San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has filed an appeal against a fine he received from the NFL this week, after the league said he had imitated swigging a beer during an on-field celebration. The incident happened during the Niners' 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins, during which Juszczyk tipped his head back and mimed taking a celebratory sip, which the 10-times Pro Bowler later said was a nod to his nickname "Juice". The NFL saw it differently, confirming reports that the gesture was seen as mimicking drinking beer, which breaks rules forbidding engaging in offensive demonstrations. The league also confirmed reports that Juszczyk had appealed the fine. ESPN's NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that the Harvard grad texted him: "I don’t even drink beer!" The 35-year-old also made his case on social media, posting several examples of him doing the same celebration, including one with the caption "Fresh squeezed juice". "Name is…Juice," he wrote in another post on Instagram.

View this post on Instagram

item.title: Petróleo fecha em alta de cerca de 3% após ataque dos houthis à Arábia Saudita
item.description: Os preços do petróleo subiram cerca de 3% nesta quinta-feira, atingindo a maior cotação em uma semana, depois que um ataque com mísseis dos houthis contra a Arábia Saudita reacendeu os temores de interrupções no abastecimento.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo subiram cerca de 3% nesta quinta-feira, atingindo a maior cotação em uma semana, depois que um ataque com mísseis dos houthis contra a Arábia Saudita reacendeu os temores de interrupções no abastecimento. No entanto, as negociações foram voláteis e os preços recuaram em relação às máximas do pregão após notícias de que os EUA e o Irã discutiram a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz. Os futuros do Brent subiram US$3,52, ou 3,4%, fechando a US$106,60 o barril. O petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA subiu US$2,45, ou 2,7%, fechando a US$ 94,61. Em suas máximas da sessão, ambos os contratos registraram alta de cerca de 5%. O Brent registrou seu maior fechamento desde 15 de setembro. Foi a primeira alta em dias para o WTI, que havia caído 13% nas seis sessões anteriores. A Arábia Saudita interceptou seis mísseis balísticos disparados pelos houthis do Iêmen, apoiados pelo Irã, frustrando ataques à província de Taif, no sul do país, e à região de Yanbu, no Mar Vermelho, informou a coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita no Iêmen. Companhias aéreas iranianas foram proibidas de operar em países vizinhos, incluindo os Emirados Árabes Unidos e Omã, em resposta às novas sanções dos EUA -- o primeiro grande impacto de uma mudança na política norte-americana para atingir empresas de países terceiros que fazem negócios com o Irã. Com a guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã praticamente estagnada há meses no campo de batalha, Washington anunciou uma extensão de suas sanções financeiras, visando empresas de países terceiros que fazem negócios com empresas iranianas -- uma prática conhecida como “sanções secundárias”. Na quarta-feira, o Irã ameaçou retaliar contra os países vizinhos que cumprirem a proibição dos EUA aos seus voos, tornando seus aeroportos “inutilizáveis”. Por outro lado, a Arábia Saudita está aumentando os volumes de bombeamento de petróleo por meio de seu oleoduto Leste-Oeste, que se estende até Yanbu, seu centro de exportação no Mar Vermelho, embora os carregamentos de petroleiros ainda não tenham sido retomados, de acordo com fontes do setor, imagens de satélite e dados de transporte marítimo.

item.title: Late Gakpo equaliser earns Dutch 1-1 draw against Germany to spoil Klopp's debut
item.description: Cody Gakpo volleyed in a stoppage-time equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying new coach Juergen Klopp a winning start.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cody Gakpo volleyed in a stoppage-time equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying new coach Juergen Klopp a winning start. Former Liverpool manager Klopp, who [USN:L1N43Q095 TEXT:"took charge of"] Germany in July following their shock early World Cup exit following defeat by Paraguay, looked to have made a winning start before Gakpo rounded off a quick counter-attack. That gave new Netherlands coach, Xavi Hernandez, appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following their World Cup round of 32 elimination, something to smile about. Xavi is the first foreigner in charge of the Dutch national team since the 1978 World Cup. "We have to accept the result," Klopp said. "Even though I badly wanted to win I take the draw." "I was very, very, very pleased with a lot of the individual performances. Overall, I was very happy with the passion we showed. We can play better and play more football, that’s for sure," he said. The Germans got bad news before the start with playmaker Jamal Musiala ruled out after feeling muscle pain during the warm-up, but they still made a high-tempo start. They were left stunned in the 13th minute when Dutch captain Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner but his effort was overruled by VAR for a foul on Germany keeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen. There was more bad news for Klopp's team with forward Kai Havertz taken off injured in the 30th, but the visitors took the lead two minutes later with Felix Nmecha slotting in from close range. Karim Adeyemi should have scored again but he somehow missed the target from five metres out. The Dutch upped the pressure after the break and repeatedly came close to an equaliser with Germany's new number one Ter Stegen making several good saves. But their dominance finally paid off with Gakpo's late strike. "We deserved at least a point," van Dijk said. "We played well at times.. but after only three days working it was a good performance." HAALAND WINNER In their Scandinavian Group A4 clash, Norway's Erling Haaland struck twice, including a 74th-minute winner, to edge his team past Denmark 3-2 in Oslo and earn their first competitive win over their opponents. "It tasted sweet. It feels great to beat our neighbours," captain Martin Odegaard said. "There is a lot we could have done better, but even when we were put under pressure, we found a way back and responded." The Danes had powered back from a two-goal deficit and levelled on the hour after first-half goals from Oscar Bobb and Haaland had put the hosts 2-0 up. Norway were left with 10 men in stoppage time after David Moller Wolfe was sent off following a second booking. Veteran Cristiano Ronaldo had a goal disallowed but Portugal still earned a 1-0 victory over Wales courtesy of Joao Felix's 22nd minute long-range winner in a successful start for the defending Nations League champions' new coach Jorge Jesus. Wales had several golden chances in the second half and hit the crossbar through Brennan Johnson before Portugal defender Ruben Dias made two key blocks to protect their lead. Saied Abu Farchi scored in the 55th minute for Israel in their League B 3-1 defeat by hosts Austria, but the player was [USN:L6N45G19K TEXT:"sent off"] after a second booking following his celebration where he simulated a gun with the corner flag. Romano Schmid had given Austria a 43rd-minute lead with a penalty and the hosts struck twice more late in the game to earn the three points. There was drama in Belgrade where visitors Greece came from a goal down to snatch a 2-1 victory over Serbia thanks to Tasos Douvikas' winner deep in stoppage time. French-born players scored every goal as Malta came from behind to beat Andorra 2-1 in their Nations League D clash. Irvin Cardona and Teddy Teuma took turns as scorer and provider to secure Malta’s victory after fellow French-born forward Guillaume Lopez had put the hosts ahead.

item.title: パレスチナ議長、20年ぶり評議会選実施を再表明 国連総会でビデオ演説
item.description:
Nidal al-Mughrabi Ali Sawafta
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nidal al-Mughrabi　Ali Sawafta

[２４日　ロイター] - パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長は２４日、ニューヨークで開かれている国連総会の一般討論でビデオ演説し、立法評議会（議会）選挙を１１月２８日に実施する計画を改めて表明した。実現すれば約２０年ぶりの選挙となる。国内では実施を疑問視する見方が根強いものの、国際社会が支持する改革を前進させる狙いがある。

アッバス氏は、「われわれは国民と国際社会に対して約束した国家改革計画を完了させた」と説明。その上で「１１月２８日の立法評議会選挙に向けて前進している」と述べた。

アッバス氏は、汚職や統治の問題に対処するための改革を実施するよう米国から圧力を受けており、米国側は同氏がこうした改革を実行してこなかったと非難している。

パレスチナでは、２００５─０６年の選挙以降、評議会選挙も議長選も実施されていない。その後、イスラム組織ハマスがパレスチナ自治区ガザを掌握し、アッバス氏の側近らを追放した。アッバス氏は今年、２０２７年に議長選挙を実施するとの議長令を出したが、具体的な日程はまだ決まっていない。

一方、アッバス氏が率いる自治政府主流派ファタハ幹部らは、選挙の実施を疑問視している。同氏は立法評議会選挙の実施を約束している一方で、ファタハ内部からの要請を含め、議長選の実施を求める声には応じていない。

アッバス氏はまた、パレスチナ代表団の国連本部への立ち入りを制限した米国の措置を批判し、開催国としての義務違反だと非難。米国が自身へのビザ発給を再び拒否したことにも言及し、「われわれはこうした違法な懲罰的措置と、その根拠となる非難や正当化を拒絶する」と述べた。

item.title: Finnish leader pleads with Musk to help Ukraine hit Russian missile launchers
item.description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said on Thursday he pleaded with SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage for Ukraine so it can strike Russian ballistic missile launchers located inside Russian territory.
item.dc:creator: Tom Balmforth
item.content:encoded: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said on Thursday he pleaded with SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage for Ukraine so it can strike Russian ballistic missile launchers located inside Russian territory. With winter looming, Ukraine has an acute shortage of air defenses to repel Russian ballistic missiles, and Kyiv officials believe that turning on Starlink over Russian territory would help it target the Russian launchers that fire the missiles. "That's why ... I plead that Elon Musk would give the Ukrainians the possibility to use Starlink in areas where there are ballistic missile launchers, either in the occupied territory of Ukraine or in Russia for strategic purposes because that would save lives," Stubb said. The Finnish leader, a staunch ally of Ukraine who also has good relations with US President Donald Trump, made the remark in an interview with Reuters in New York where world leaders have converged for the annual gathering at the United Nations. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy used the event to press hard for [USN:L1N45F0K5 TEXT:"ceasefires"] that would cover strikes on targets related to energy infrastructure and vessels in the Black Sea. Russia has given no public indication it wants to see such arrangements. Four-and-a-half years since the full-scale Russian invasion, the Ukrainians fear Moscow plans to systematically target and destroy power and heating sites in the depth of winter. Russia's use of ballistic missiles hit record levels this summer. Only Ukraine's Patriot air defenses are able to intercept such missiles, but ammunition is severely depleted and it is unclear where new supplies could come from. Musk switched on the Starlink satellite internet service over Ukraine shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. It has become the lifeblood of Ukraine's battlefield communications and a tool for piloting drones. Starlink does not work over Russian territory, but Ukrainian officials believe turning it on for Ukraine's use inside Russia would allow its weapons to strike mobile ballistic launchers located within several hundred kilometres of the border. Looking ahead to winter, Stubb said there were three things that Ukraine needed. "One is air defenses and even Starlink would be to a certain extent a good air defense there. And the second one is energy installations for the winter." "The third one is money. So those are the things that we're working on. We're working on putting up a winter package because I don't see the war ending, you know, before the winter." Stubb said it was good that US-led peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine had restarted in August with the visits of US envoys to both Moscow and Kyiv. "I still think that the easiest solution would be to call an unconditional ceasefire, basically stop the killing, as President Trump reiterated in his speech in the UN General Assembly," he said. Such a step, he continued, would be followed by negotiations on security, territory, reconstruction and compensation and other topics. The war could be frozen along the line of contact with 30-kilometre buffer zones east and west, he said, adding that the next best option was the idea of the partial ceasefire on energy and grain related targets.

item.title: White Sox rout Royals, clinch first playoff berth since 2021
item.description: Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth. Chicago (82-77) is back in the AL postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons. Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hander Randy Dobnak, the White Sox moved to a half-game behind the Central Division-leading Cleveland Guardians, who were set to play in Boston later Thursday. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland and is 3½ games up on the Texas Rangers for the third and final AL wild-card berth. The White Sox scored three runs in each of the first two innings against Kansas City (68-91). Vargas and Tristan Peters contributed RBI singles in the first inning while Vargas added another run-scoring single in the second. Sandlin, a rookie righty, pitched comfortably with the lead. He worked around Bobby Witt Jr.'s one-out double to escape the first inning in 17 pitches and needed 85 pitches to complete his outing. Sandlin (3-2) yielded one run and five hits with zero walks against seven strikeouts. Dobnak (3-5) allowed six runs (four earned) and six hits in 1 1/3 innings. He had one walk and one strikeout while throwing a wild pitch and committing an error on a pickoff attempt. Teel reached reliever Alex Lange for a solo shot to start the fourth and Peters had an RBI forceout later in the inning. Salvador Perez homered leading off the bottom of the fourth to bring the Royals to within 8-1. It marked Perez's 20th round-tripper this season, his sixth consecutive campaign reaching that plateau. John Rave and Jason Isbel had two hits apiece for Kansas City. Witt Jr. has reached base in 21 consecutive games. Sam Antonacci, Chase Meidroth, Braden Montgomery and Teel joined Vargas with two-hit efforts for Chicago. Andrew Benintendi and Peters also had two RBIs. Chicago won the season series from Kansas City 9-4. The White Sox have won four of five while the Royals have lost six of seven. --Field Level Media

item.title: Inside Reuters' calculation of Australia's housing market ripple effects
item.description: For most Australian homeowners, the cost of the country's sharpest housing downturn in years has been the modest fall in property values since interest rates began rising in February.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: For most Australian homeowners, the cost of the country's sharpest housing downturn in years has been the modest fall in property values since interest rates began rising in February. But while prices have dipped only slightly, home sales have fallen sharply. Reuters set out to [USN:L4N45008Y TEXT:"measure the impact"] on the businesses that depend on housing turnover. Those businesses span a vast ecosystem built during Australia's quarter-century property boom. Real estate agents, conveyancers, auctioneers, property listing sites, furniture stagers and building inspectors largely earn revenue when homes change hands. Removalists, painters, landscapers, renovators and furniture retailers are also exposed to sales activity, though they make money elsewhere too. To estimate the economic impact, Reuters calculated the commercial spending typically generated when an Australian sells a home, buys another and moves. The analysis covered costs from agent commissions and listing preparations through settlement, moving expenses and purchases of furniture and appliances. Low and high estimates of individual goods were used to derive an impact range. State governments were excluded, despite collecting large stamp-duty revenues and seeing their [USN:L4N4570GO TEXT:"revenue hit"] by the slowdown, because they are not commercial entities. Banks were also excluded because most housing-related earnings come from mortgage repayments rather than transaction volumes. The analysis was based on Australia's median home price of A$1.11 million ($790,000) and the most common dwelling type, a three-bedroom detached house. For each good or service, Reuters used a mainstream advertised price range rather than extreme outliers. Agent commissions, for example, were assumed at the common 2% to 3% range. A new couch might cost anywhere from A$20 on Marketplace to A$60,000 from an exclusive boutique. Instead, we used the cheapest widely available option (A$219 from Kogan.com.au) and the priciest mainstream offering (A$8,796 from King Furniture), applying the same methodology across all items. Each item was then weighted by the likelihood of the expense occurring. Costs nearly universal to a transaction, such as agent commissions and conveyancing settled on software platform PEXA, received a 100% weighting. Less common expenses received lower weightings. For example, painting a three-bedroom home before sale typically costs A$4,500 to A$10,000, but a 2023 Houzz survey found only a quarter of sellers do so. Pre-sale painting was therefore weighted at 25%. Based on feedback from economists, Reuters also adjusted for the roughly 60-40 split between owner-occupiers and investors. A survey by removalist website Muval found 39% of Australians bought entertainment appliances when moving home, but only about 60% of property purchases are made by owner-occupiers. Television purchases were therefore weighted at 23%. Economists also pointed to the "wealth effect" whereby people spend less when they believe their home's value is falling. We excluded that from our analysis because the project focused solely on spending directly linked to property transactions. Some effects, after all, are much harder to measure. ($1 = 1.4088 Australian dollars)

item.title: Billions in collateral damage: The hidden cost of Australia's housing slowdown
item.description: This time last year, Sydney property stylist Joanne Cauchi was turning away work, buying new furniture and overseeing home installations almost every day.
item.dc:creator: Byron Kaye, Stella Qiu
item.content:encoded: This time last year, Sydney property stylist Joanne Cauchi was turning away work, buying new furniture and overseeing home installations almost every day. Now, her team of three stylists and two removalists handles as few as three jobs a week and has stopped buying inventory altogether. "Usually springtime, and this time of year in particular, is ridiculously busy," said Cauchi. "It is very quiet." The abrupt slowdown illustrates how Australia's housing slump is rippling far beyond real estate agents and mortgage lenders. As higher interest rates and the government's rollback of key property tax concessions sap demand, a sharp drop in home sales is hitting a vast ecosystem of businesses that rely on properties changing hands, from furniture stylists and landscapers to conveyancers, removalists and painters. The damage stems less from falling prices than from a sharp drop in turnover. Home prices are down less than 4% from their March peak and remain above year-ago levels, but far fewer homes are changing hands. A 15% drop in housing turnover since June from a year earlier is stripping an estimated A$355 million to A$710 million ($253 million to $505 million) a month from the property-adjacent economy, according to [USN:L4N45E08X TEXT:"a Reuters analysis"] of the spending triggered when Australians buy, sell and move into a home. Even allowing for annual market swings, housing turnover remains 10.5% below its five-year average, data from property consultant Cotality showed. Reuters calculations suggest that translates into A$2.8 billion to A$5.6 billion less annual spending flowing through businesses that depend on homes changing hands, from furniture retailers and tradespeople to small conveyancing firms. The figure pales beside Australia's A$600 billion-plus annual home sales, but for numerous businesses that depend on housing turnover, it is substantial. The analysis estimated the cost of the goods and services typically purchased when an average three-bedroom detached home changes hands, based on market price ranges and weighted spending patterns from industry or government data. "You get this big dollar number of 'this is how much loss to the economy there is as a result of those lost home purchases'," said James Graham, a University of Sydney senior lecturer who studies housing economics. Graham said the Reuters methodology was reasonable but noted it excluded the "wealth effect", where falling home values weigh on spending by denting confidence. A typical Australian home move triggers spending across a wide range of services, from agents to conveyancers to painters and utility providers, with buyers often also purchasing new furniture and appliances after relocating. "All of the real estate sectors are going to have less income coming in," Graham said. QUICK HIT Property's outsized role in Australia's economy was entrenched by tax incentives introduced over the past quarter century, helping drive Sydney and Melbourne into the ranks of the world's least affordable housing markets. After three interest rate increases since February, the centre-left government took further heat out of the housing market by trimming capital gains tax breaks for existing-home sellers and tightening negative-gearing rules for landlords. A spokesperson for Treasurer Jim Chalmers did not respond to a request for comment. Home sales volumes, which had risen in March, were down 11% in May and 20% in July, according to Cotality. "It's the most severe drop we've seen since the very start of COVID," said Russell Cohen, CEO of conveyancing technology platform PEXA (PXA.AX) , which gets paid when an Australian property sale settles. After growing Australian sales 8% in the year to June, volumes dived 15% in July and stayed there through August, Cohen said in an interview. The slowdown is also hurting corporate earnings. Homewares chain Harvey Norman (HVN.AX) said franchise profit in its June half fell 15%, reversing growth of 14% in the previous six months, citing "reduced appetite for home-related purchases and renovation activity". EXODUS For many businesses, the downturn is already forcing painful choices. At The Moving Box Company, which supplies new and used freight cartons, four factory-floor workers have left since April after having their hours reduced. Headcount has fallen to 9 from 13, leaving managers to take on packing and delivery work themselves. "That's practically how we've had to manage the situation: by reducing the hours of staff," said general manager James Wotherspoon, noting sales were down 19% since June year-on-year. "If we can't give them the hours, I totally respect the fact that they've got to find work elsewhere to survive." For conveyancers and selling agents, the downturn has coincided with the introduction of anti-money laundering rules in July that require greater customer due diligence, adding compliance costs just as revenue is falling. "We're definitely seeing more conversations being had from smaller operators about merging or selling, some retiring out of the industry entirely," said David Winning, founder of Your Move Conveyancing and director of the Australian Institute of Conveyancers NSW Division. The Real Estate Institute of Victoria said 350 of 6,600 agent members planned to cancel their membership, with more than half leaving the profession altogether. "We could expect to see a very significant exodus of sales agents," said Jacob Caine, president of the Real Estate Institute of Australia, by phone. Buyers' agent Zoran Solano said he was ending his office lease and would work remotely after revenue halved since May. "Everyone is being affected," he said. "It's much more widespread than I think people realise." ($1 = 1.4057 Australian dollars)

item.title: Roblox loses bid to halt L.A. County's lawsuit alleging child sex exploitation on gaming platform
item.description: Los Angeles County’s lawsuit accusing Roblox of failing to protect young users from online predators and sexual exploitation will move forward after a judge found that neither federal law nor the US Constitution’s free speech protections shield the gaming platform from the claims.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles County’s lawsuit accusing Roblox (RBLX.N) of failing to protect young users from online predators and sexual exploitation will move forward after a judge found that neither federal law nor the US Constitution’s free speech protections shield the gaming platform from the claims. Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Dean Kitchens on Wednesday rejected Roblox’s bid to dismiss the lawsuit, which alleges Roblox does little to check its users’ ages, allowing kids and adults to interact on its platform with little oversight. Claims about Roblox’s limited age verification are not barred by Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, a federal law protecting online services from liability for user content, because they don’t involve posts on the site by third parties, the judge wrote. Roblox’s choices about how to verify its users’ ages are not expressive features of the platform that would be protected by the US Constitution’s First Amendment, he added. Representatives for Roblox and the county did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Earlier this year, [USN:L4N40T18S TEXT:"Roblox said"] it was making nationwide changes to how teens and children can use its site. In part, the company said it was making changes to its age verification procedures, implementing facial age checks for chat access and introducing age-based accounts with more restrictions and expanding parental controls. A PUBLIC NUISANCE Los Angeles County filed the lawsuit in February. It claims Roblox contributed to an increase in child sex trafficking and exploitation. The county accuses the platform of misleading consumers about its safety and creating a public nuisance by exposing children to sexual exploitation. Public nuisance claims traditionally have targeted conduct that endangers public health or safety, but state governments have increasingly invoked them in litigation involving tobacco, opioids, climate change and vaping. Public nuisance cases allow governments like Los Angeles County to seek court orders forcing companies to make changes to make their products safer, as well as large financial awards to abate the alleged harm. Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin, a Republican, filed a similar public nuisance lawsuit against Roblox in June. That case, which also names chat platform Discord as a defendant, is filed in Los Angeles Superior Court and is ongoing, court records show. Earlier this year, Roblox [USN:L6N41416J TEXT:"struck settlements"] with the attorneys general of Alabama, West Virginia and Nevada, who were investigating the platform for failing to protect young users, but had not yet filed lawsuits. The company agreed to pay more than $30 million and make changes to children's access to its gaming and chat functions. DOZENS OF OTHER CASES Roblox and Discord are facing more than 180 lawsuits filed by people who say they were sexually abused or exploited as minors or filed by their parents, alleging the company failed to warn of the risk and did not take action to protect its young users. The lawsuits allege that conversations between adults and minors that began on Roblox often migrated to Discord. Both companies say they shouldn't be liable for the actions of third parties. As the Los Angeles County litigation moves closer to trial, Roblox and Discord have made efforts to move the individual cases into arbitration. In court filings this week, the companies argued that users agreed to resolve disputes outside of court when they agreed to the sites’ terms and conditions. Lawyers for the people suing say their clients deserve their day in court and will oppose the efforts to send the cases to arbitration. The Los Angeles case is The People of the State of California, acting by and through Los Angeles County Counsel Dawyn Harrison v. Roblox Corp, case number 26STCV05708 in Los Angeles Superior Court. For LA County: Alexandra Walsh of Anapol Weiss For Roblox: Andy Pincus of Mayer Brown

item.title: Trading Day: Rout of control
item.description: The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields around the world to new multi-decade highs. Stock markets around the world felt the heat, although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq staged late rallies to end flat, while oil and the dollar marched higher.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields around the world to new multi-decade highs. Stock markets around the world felt the heat, although the [USN:L6N45G0LR TEXT:"S&P 500 and Nasdaq"] staged late rallies to end flat, while [USN:L6N45G01N TEXT:"oil"] and the [USN:L4N45G03F TEXT:"dollar"] marched higher. In [USN:L6N45F0XH TEXT:"my column today"], I look at the dollar's resurgence and soaring bond yields in the context of the US Treasury's recent forays into the FX and bond markets. Right now, "the house" — as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent referred to himself recently — is not winning. Today's Key Reads [USN:FWN45G0T8 TEXT:"Trump says he'll discuss AI with Xi but wants to 'leave it exactly where it is'"] [USN:S0N43U01A TEXT:"US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal, Bessent says"] [USN:L8N45G0KO TEXT:"Global bond selloff deepens, as US 30-year yields hit highest since 2004"] [USN:L1N45F0NE TEXT:"US weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows; price reductions boost new home sales"] [USN:L8N45G133 TEXT:"ECB's Schnabel quits to join IMF, setting in motion a board reshuffle"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: MSCI Asia ex-Japan -0.9%, [USN:L6N45G0EZ TEXT:"Europe"] -0.6%, Wall Street mixed: S&P 500 and Nasdaq flat, Dow -0.3% and a 3-month low. SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Utilities, materials -1%. Comms services +2%. Walmart, IBM -2.5%. Disney +2%. [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"Oracle and Blue Owl"] both down ~3.5%. FX: [USN:L4N45G03F TEXT:"Dollar"] hits two-month high, dollar/yen flirts with 159.00. Colombian peso -2%. [USN:L1N45G096 TEXT:"Norwegian, Swedish"] crowns steady after rate decisions. BONDS: French, German yields highest since 2007-08, US 30y yield highest since 2004. US 7y auction weak. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L6N45G01N TEXT:"Oil"] up ~3%, [USN:L4N45G01B TEXT:"gold"] slips ~1%.

Today's Talking Points: No, Mr Bond, I expect you to die The global bond selloff got ugly this week. The rise in yields on Wednesday — ostensibly for "good" reasons of strong business activity data — was exceptional, and pointed to a more worrying breakdown in sentiment. There was little relief on Thursday. Yields are at multi-decade highs in the US, Europe and Japan, but this isn't drawing in buyers en masse. Bond market volatility is now surging too, another reason many investors might sit it out a bit longer. Demand at yesterday's 5-year US bond auction was the lowest in nine years, and the premium demanded by buyers who did show up was one of the highest ever. Today's 7-year auction was also extremely weak. As BofA analysts put it, "the price action likely highlights that investors are not yet comfortable owning bonds in the environment of a Fed restarting the hiking cycle, continued conflict in the Middle East, and a resilient US economy and consumer." An unbridgeable US-China gap Huge fanfare, pomp, and ceremony, but not much substance when it comes to the big issues of the day. Is that a harsh but fair assessment of how the Trump-Xi summit will pan out? True, the US-China trade truce could be extended for another two months to January, and the two sides will agree to further dialogue on AI. But from a market and investment perspective, that's about it. One ironic market curiosity: it is perhaps fitting that on the day Trump and Xi tried to bridge divides and close gaps between the two superpowers, the spread between the two countries' bond yields widened to a record 350 basis points. US borrowing costs are soaring in the face of high inflation, while China’s are sliding as the threat of deflation continues to stalk the economy. Neither side is "winning" on that front. Data center blues Oracle on Thursday declared [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:""force majeure""] on a massive AI data center project, seeking to protect itself from soaring costs from potential delays in securing power for the "Project Jupiter" venture in New Mexico. Oracle's credit rating sits one notch above junk, and its total debt stands at around $140 billion. Shares fell to a seven-week low on Thursday. But this goes well beyond Oracle. The industry-wide AI capex spend runs into the trillions of dollars, and is increasingly being financed by debt, leasing and other off-balance sheet structures. Many investors were already nervous about the vast cost of building the data centers needed to power the artificial intelligence revolution. This potentially pours fuel on these flames. What could move markets tomorrow? Chinese President Xi Jinping visits US President Donald Trump in Washington Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey speaks US University of Michigan inflation expectations, consumer sentiment (September, final) US durable goods (August) US Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include New York Fed President John Williams, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack Want to receive Trading Day in your inbox every weekday morning? Sign up for my newsletter here . Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: Cubs lock up playoff berth with win over Marlins
item.description: Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping the host Chicago Cubs clinch a playoff berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping the host Chicago Cubs clinch a playoff berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday afternoon. Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong walked to lead off the first inning and promptly stole second base to become the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in a single season. Armstrong, who has 45 homers, joined Jose Canseco (1988), Barry Bonds (1996), Alex Rodriguez (1998), Alfonso Soriano (2006), Ronald Acuna Jr. (2023) and Shohei Ohtani (2024) as the only players to reach the 40-40 milestone. Seiya Suzuki belted a solo homer in the fifth inning to highlight his two-hit performance for the Cubs (88-71), who salvaged the finale of their three-game series with Miami. Boyd (10-5) allowed one run on five hits to record his second straight victory following a 0-4 stretch over his previous six starts. Daniel Palencia bridged the gap to Ryan Zeferjahn, who retired the side in order in the ninth inning to secure his seventh save of the season. Jakob Marsee had an RBI single in the third inning for the Marlins (78-81), who have lost four of their last six games. With the game tied 1-1, Ian Happ tripled off Jack Ralston (0-2) to lead off the sixth inning and came home on Hoerner's RBI single to left field. Ralston permitted two runs on three hits in 1 1/3 innings. Brian Navarreto doubled to lead off the third inning against Matthew Boyd before coming home on Marsee's RBI single to center to open the scoring. Suzuki forged a tie in the fifth inning, depositing a 1-0 pitch from Ralston over the wall in center field. The homer was Suzuki's 26th of the season and second in his last four games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Presidente Peña anuncia inversión de 200 millones de dólares para proyecto forestal en Paraguay
item.description: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, anunció el jueves en Nueva York una inversión de 200 millones de dólares de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital y el grupo local Robinson para un proyecto forestal que se lanzará en el primer trimestre de 2027 en el país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, anunció el jueves en Nueva York una inversión de 200 millones de dólares de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital y el grupo local Robinson para un proyecto forestal que se lanzará en el primer trimestre de 2027 en el país. La inversión considera el establecimiento de bosques comerciales, la restauración de bosques nativos y la producción sostenible de madera de alta calidad, según un comunicado de la presidencia paraguaya. La iniciativa prevé el desarrollo en una primera etapa de cerca de 20.000 hectáreas destinadas a la producción de madera. También apunta a la generación de créditos de carbono. "Esta inversión en Paraguay representa una oportunidad atractiva para construir una plataforma forestal escalable y de largo plazo, basada en la gestión sostenible de los recursos y el desarrollo rural", señaló Angela Davis, CEO de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital, según el comunicado.

item.title: Peso mexicano cae a mínimos desde abril tras decisión de Banxico
item.description: El peso mexicano se debilitó el jueves a niveles no vistos en más de cinco meses, luego de que Banco de México mantuvo sin cambios su tasa clave de interés y señaló que sus próximas decisiones dependerán de la evolución de la inflación local.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se debilitó el jueves a niveles no vistos en más de cinco meses, luego de que [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"Banco de México"] mantuvo sin cambios su tasa clave de interés y señaló que sus próximas decisiones dependerán de la evolución de la inflación local. La autoridad indicó, además, que no reaccionará de forma mecánica a las decisiones de la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"] estadounidense, que elevó la semana pasada su tasa en 25 puntos básicos y proyectó al menos otro incremento antes de finalizar el año. * La moneda local se negociaba en 17.7448 por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una pérdida de un 1.3%, aunque poco antes llegó a depreciarse hasta 17.7710 unidades, su nivel más débil desde inicios de abril. * El declive estuvo acompañado por un fortalecimiento global de la [USN:L1N45G0Z4 TEXT:"divisa estadounidense"] que tocó máximos de dos meses, mientras que los [USN:L6N45G14L TEXT:"precios del petróleo"] subieron, después de que un ataque con misiles de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita reavivó el temor a una interrupción del suministro mundial. * A nivel doméstico, el mensaje de Banxico reforzó la expectativa de que mantendrá la tasa clave sin cambios durante un periodo prolongado. Un [USN:L6N45D0SW TEXT:"sondeo de Reuters"] mostró el lunes que el mercado anticipa que el banco central mexicano la conservará estable al menos hasta la segunda mitad de 2028. * En cambio, una ola de comentarios recientes de funcionarios de la Fed, incluidos [USN:L6N45G0KQ TEXT:"John Williams"], [USN:L6N45G0UM TEXT:"Beth Hammack"] y [USN:L6N45G0XB TEXT:"Anna Paulson"] el jueves, afianzaron la perspectiva de que podrían requerirse más alzas de tasas en Estados Unidos para contener la inflación. * La atención de los inversionistas está puesta así en el diferencial de rendimientos entre México y Estados Unidos, un factor que por largo tiempo ha impulsado la entrada de flujos a los mercados locales desde el exterior. * En el frente externo, la sesión estuvo marcada por el comienzo de una cumbre entre el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y a su par chino, [USN:L8N45G1N5 TEXT:"Xi Jinping"], en la Casa Blanca. * La bolsa, por su parte, recortó parte de sus pérdidas iniciales y cerró prácticamente estable. El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) bajó un marginal 0.02% a 64,264.16 puntos, en línea con una jornada de vaivenes en [USN:L1N45G11H TEXT:"Wall Sreet"]. * Las acciones del operador bursátil Grupo BMV (BOLSAA.MX) fueron las que mostraron el peor desempeño, al caer un 2.19% a 38.05 pesos. Por el contrario, los títulos del grupo aeroportuario GAP (GAPB.MX) ganaron un 2.69% a 374.78 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años subió ocho puntos base a un 9.45%, mientras que la tasa a 20 años ascendió cinco, a un 9.85%.

item.title: 原油先物3％高、フーシ派のサウジ攻撃で供給不安が再燃
item.description:
Scott DiSavino
[ニューヨーク ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Scott DiSavino

[ニューヨーク ２４日 ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は、約３％上昇し１週間ぶりの高値を付けた。フーシ派によるサウジアラビアへのミサイル攻撃を受けて供給混乱への懸念が再燃した。

取引は不安定で、米国とイランがホルムズ海峡の再開について協議していると報じられたのを受け、価格は取引時間中の高値から後退した。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．５２ドル（３．４％）高の１バレル＝１０６．６０ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は２．４５ドル（２．７％）高の９４．６１ドル。取引時間中の高値では、両限月ともに約５％上昇していた。

イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２４日、サウジアラビアの首都リヤドの「重要目標」と、紅海沿岸都市ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設をミサイルと無人機（ドローン）で攻撃したと表明した。

サウジ主導の連合はこの日、フーシ派が２４日に発射した弾道ミサイル６発を迎撃し、南部タイフと紅海沿岸のヤンブー地区への攻撃を阻止したと明らかにしていた。

item.title: Five takeaways from Trump's summit with Xi in Washington
item.description: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday, with talks on trade and artificial intelligence and the growing strategic rivalry between the countries all in the spotlight during an elaborate state visit.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Trevor Hunnicutt, David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday, with talks on trade and artificial intelligence and the growing strategic rivalry between the countries all in the spotlight during an elaborate state visit. Here are some major takeaways from the talks: TRADE DEAL EXTENDED, FOR NOW The US secured an extension of its trade truce this week - but only a short one. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides agreed to extend by two months a trade agreement that ended last year's trade war and was due to expire in November. The extension would give Washington and Beijing "more time to see what we can do on the economic front," he said. But rather than locking in a durable agreement, the extension appears to push the central questions — tariffs, Chinese purchases, rare-earth supplies and technology restrictions — into the next round of negotiations. Bessent said on Wednesday that Beijing was meeting its requirement in the earlier agreement to buy 25 million tons of soybeans but was lagging on its pledge to buy $17 billion in other agricultural goods. US officials have said rare-earth deliveries were also falling short, another sign that significant gaps remain. For companies, the result is a familiar form of instability: tariff rates remain lower for now, but decisions must still be made against a shifting policy backdrop. DRESS TO IMPRESS For Trump, Xi's White House visit was an opportunity to show off a Washington being remade in his image. After Xi treated Trump in Beijing to a tour around a Ming dynasty temple and a walled-off garden retreat rarely opened to foreigners, the US president returned the favor with a different kind of spectacle: Troops wearing wigs and tri-corner hats marched in formation and played music in a Rose Garden redesigned to look like a Trump golf club. Fighter jets and bombers roared overhead during ceremonies staged on Wednesday and Thursday, one so loud it caused Trump to flinch. When the White House press corps was called to cover the two leaders, it wasn’t to hear them talk about the weighty affairs of state. Instead, it was to watch them tour the Marine One helicopter and the recently redesigned South Lawn of the White House, replete with a large helipad emblazoned with the presidential seal. Speaking to reporters, Trump brushed away questions about their policy discussions. “He loves good granite,” Trump said of Xi. “Great meeting.” XI WANTS US 'PRUDENCE' OVER TAIWAN As expected, Xi pressed Trump on the Taiwan issue, saying, according to China's official news agency, that China hoped the United States would "handle the Taiwan question with prudence." The agency's English-language service also wrote that Xi hoped the US would oppose Taiwan independence. That would be a tougher version of Washington's long-standing formulation that it does not "support" independence. There are no signs that the Trump administration plans to change its wording. There was no immediate White House readout of the exchange, but US officials have long avoided explicitly stating opposition to Taiwanese independence. Any shift in language would raise questions about Washington's resolve to defend the island and provoke opposition in Congress. STRATEGIC RISK Xi, not for the first time while meeting Trump, invoked the "Thucydides Trap", an academic theory that competition between a rising power and an established one tends toward war. While the Chinese leader said the risk "can be overcome," his reference underscored how concerns about a potential US-China military conflict continue to shadow relations between the world's two largest powers. Xi argued that both nations stand to gain from cooperation and lose from confrontation, and he called for regular military dialogue and stronger crisis-prevention mechanisms. Trump, for his part, drew on the two nations' shared history to emphasize the potential for cooperation. They could accomplish much by pursuing common interests, he said, invoking their wartime alliance against Japan. DIFFERENCES ON AI The two leaders expressed diverging views about artificial intelligence. Trump, who has declared that AI should be called super intelligence, or SI, said in a social media post that he wants to “to leave it exactly where it is" and rely on the US Department of Justice rather than impose any new guardrails. He insisted that China held the same position. But Xi said on Thursday that, as leading nations on AI, China and the US must manage its growth. “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people,” Xi said. Some of the biggest names in AI were expected to attend Trump's [USN:L1N45E0H3 TEXT:"state dinner"] at the White House on Thursday for Xi, including Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang.

item.title: US law firm Duane Morris settles ex-partner's lawsuit over pay
item.description: US law firm Duane Morris has agreed to resolve a lawsuit that accused the firm of misclassifying some of its employees as partners in a bid to force them to pay part of the firm's taxes and expenses while denying them a share of its profits.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella, David Thomas
item.content:encoded: US law firm Duane Morris has agreed to resolve a lawsuit that accused the firm of misclassifying some of its employees as partners in a bid to force them to pay part of the firm's taxes and expenses while denying them a share of its profits. The firm and plaintiff Meagan Garland said in a filing in federal court in California on Wednesday that they reached an accord after mediation and were hashing out the terms. Duane Morris had no immediate comment, and a lawyer for Garland did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Garland, who was previously a partner in the firm's employment practice, filed the [USN:L1N3JO14Q TEXT:"proposed class action lawsuit"] against Duane Morris in August 2024. She alleged the Philadelphia-based firm was misclassifying its non-equity partners as "partners" even though they can be hired and fired at-will, and do not have an ownership stake in the firm. Many US law firms internally designate some partners as non-equity or "income" partners. Such partners typically earn far less than full equity partners, whose compensation is tied directly to firm profits. Several major law firms in recent years have [USN:L1N3LM0MX TEXT:"created non-equity partnership tiers"]. After promoting lower-ranked lawyers to its non-equity partner tier, Duane Morris ceases paying the employer's share of their federal and state payroll taxes, as well as their benefits such as health care, vision, dental and disability insurance, Garland alleged. Duane Morris in a court filing had denied any wrongdoing and said Garland was a "genuine partner whom the firm has always compensated and otherwise treated fairly and well within the bounds of the law." US District Judge Cathy Ann Bencivengo in San Diego last year [USN:L1N3TW0SY TEXT:"denied the law firm's bid"] to dismiss most of the claims in the lawsuit. The case is Meagan Garland v. Duane Morris, LLP, et al., US District Court for the Southern District of California, 3:24-cv-01783 For Meagan Garland: Bibianne Fell and Marlee Horwitz of Fell Law For Duane Morris: Anthony Oncidi, Gregory Knopp, Philippe Lebel and Elise Bloom of Proskauer Rose

item.title: City Therapeutics files for US IPO as biotech listings surge
item.description: City Therapeutics filed for a US initial public offering on Thursday, joining a rush of biotech firms lining up to tap the fall IPO window.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: City Therapeutics filed for a US initial public offering on Thursday, joining a rush of biotech firms lining up to tap the fall IPO window. Biotech has been one of the key themes of the IPO market this year amid renewed investor interest in the industry, although fall listings have struggled to gain momentum as surging bond yields, a tightening rate environment and concerns around the AI trade weigh on risk appetite. "For a biotech with a promising therapeutic, a small change in interest rates or macro headwinds don't make much of a difference," said Matt Kennedy, senior ‍strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs. "It really all boils down to whether the drug candidate is successful in the clinic. That and biotech sentiment, which is still riding high despite the pressure elsewhere in the IPO market." Other drug developers [USN:L4N45A1Q0 TEXT:"Retension Pharmaceuticals, TRex Bio"] and [USN:L4N45D1EI TEXT:"Iambic Therapeutics"] earlier this month also unveiled their US IPO filings, a key step ahead of a potential roadshow launch. ADARx Pharmaceuticals, which is developing RNA-based drugs for rare diseases, is [USN:L4N45D0MS TEXT:"expected to go public"] on Friday. Founded in 2023, City Therapeutics is advancing a pipeline of RNA-based drugs for rare diseases. Its most advanced product candidate, CITY-FXI, is in an early-stage trial to treat thrombosis, which is the formation of harmful clots inside a blood vessel. The Cambridge, Massachusetts-based company has raised roughly $238.8 million since inception from life sciences investors, including ARCH Venture Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Invus, and Viking Global Investors. "Aside from positive clinical results, IPO investors are looking for partnerships with large pharmas, which can increase the likelihood of an acquisition down the road," Renaissance Capital's Kennedy said. Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, Stifel and Oppenheimer are the underwriters for the offering. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol "CTY".

item.title: US airlines oppose China's bid to add more flights
item.description: The head of industry group Airlines for America said on Thursday that US carriers oppose adding more direct flights from China to the United States even as Chinese President Xi Jinping raised the idea.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The head of industry group Airlines for America said on Thursday that US carriers oppose adding more direct flights from China to the United States even as Chinese President Xi Jinping raised the idea. Chris Sununu, who heads the group representing American Airlines (AAL.O) , United Airlines (UAL.O) , Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) and others, said US carriers continue to be hampered by the fact that Chinese counterparts are allowed to overfly Russia on eight flights. He said he has been advocating to Trump administration officials not to give in. "It's not just a minor thing. It's a huge cost to the airlines to have to go around Russia," Sununu said in an interview. At an [USN:L1N45F0US TEXT:"event in Washington"] on Thursday, Xi raised the idea of increasing flights. Currently, the United States and China each can operate around 50 round-trip flights per week. "Our two sides may also increase direct flights to facilitate two-way travel and trade," Xi said. The White House did not immediately comment. More than 150 weekly round-trip passenger flights were allowed by each side before restrictions were imposed in early 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Until August 2023, Chinese and US carriers could each fly only 12 a week between the two countries. Airlines for America last week opposed the request of Air China (601111.SS) to fly more scheduled flights because US airlines are effectively banned from flying from the US East Coast to China because they cannot access Russian airspace, while Chinese carriers can for eight US flights. "It's imbalanced. It's unfair," Sununu said. "They already have an advantage with the eight flights. To give them even more of an advantage would be huge," he said. "Don't make it worse for us." The US in March 2022 banned Russian flights from American airspace after Russia's invasion of neighboring Ukraine , which prompted Russia to ban US carriers from overflying the country. The United States has not banned other countries from overflying Russia but struck a deal with China in 2023 that additional flights approved would not do so. In October 2025, the US Transportation Department proposed banning Chinese airlines from flying over Russia on routes to and from the United States, saying the reduced flight time this practice enables puts American carriers at a disadvantage. But the proposal faced opposition from other US agencies and was shelved ahead of trade talks with China.

item.title: 米政権、オープンＡＩとアンソロピックに英への新モデル共有保留を要請＝報道
item.description: [ワシントン ２４日 ロイター] - 米ホワイトハウスが人工知能（ＡＩ）大手のオープンＡＩとアンソロピックに対し、米...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米政権、オープンＡＩとアンソロピックに英への新モデル共有保留を要請＝報道 5:41 配信

6月11日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

[ワシントン ２４日 ロイター] - 米ホワイトハウスが人工知能（ＡＩ）大手のオープンＡＩとアンソロピックに対し、米当局による審査が完了するまで、英国の試験担当者らに新ＡＩモデルを共有しないよう求めていたことが分かった。米メディアのポリティコが２４日、米政府高官や関係筋の話として報じた。

報道によると、ホワイトハウスは、パートナー国とのＡＩモデルの共有に先立ち、米国のシステムの安全性を確認するための措置を講じたい考えという。

ＡＩが外部システムに侵入するなどの「暴走」事例が相次いで報告されているほか、アンソロピックの研究者２人が、ＡＩの急速な進歩によって近い将来に「人類滅亡」につながる可能性があると警告したことを受け、ＡＩの安全性を巡る議論が活発化している。

また、オーストラリア政府は２４日、オープンＡＩが開発したＡＩエージェントが今年６月、豪政府の医療データポータルに侵入し、ファイルに不正アクセスしていたと明らかにした。

item.title: Banco Mundial aprueba 200 millones de dólares de financiación adicional a Colombia para atender terremoto
item.description: El Banco Mundial anunció el jueves que aprobó 200 millones de dólares en financiación adicional a Colombia para atender la recuperación del terremoto del 10 de agosto, que dejó cientos de muertos y billones de pesos en daños.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Banco Mundial anunció el jueves que aprobó 200 millones de dólares en financiación adicional a Colombia para atender la recuperación del terremoto del 10 de agosto, que dejó cientos de muertos y billones de pesos en daños. La financiación se suma a los 200 millones de dólares ya desembolsados a Colombia por el banco multilateral de desarrollo el 14 de agosto, en el marco de un programa anterior que incluía fondos de ayuda para desastres. El ministro de Hacienda de Colombia, Miguel Gómez, celebró la aprobación de los nuevos fondos y señaló que ayudarían a las comunidades afectadas por el terremoto. "Esta financiación adicional del Banco Mundial demuestra confianza en Colombia y en la capacidad del gobierno para responder de manera responsable en momentos difíciles", dijo en un comunicado difundido por el Banco Mundial. Los fondos proporcionarán un rápido apoyo presupuestario para atender las necesidades de reconstrucción tras el terremoto, al tiempo que continúan fortaleciendo los marcos de gestión y financiación del riesgo de desastres en Colombia, aseguró el Banco. El Banco Mundial sigue trabajando en una Evaluación Global Rápida de Daños Posdesastre (GRADE, por sus siglas en inglés), que ayudará a Colombia a priorizar la ayuda y las labores de reconstrucción. El sismo de magnitud 7,4 del 10 de agosto derribó edificios de apartamentos y causó daños en viviendas, escuelas y hospitales en una amplia región del oeste de Colombia. La semana pasada, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo estimó que el terremoto causó daños por valor de unos 14.000 millones de dólares, una cifra muy superior a la estimación preliminar del gobierno colombiano, de 9.500 millones de dólares. Las autoridades colombianas estiman que 331 personas murieron a causa del terremoto y más de 4.500 resultaron heridas.

item.title: Israel's Abu Farchi sent off after gun gesture celebration
item.description: Israel forward Saied Abu Farchi was sent off for celebrating his goal against Austria in their 3-1 UEFA Nations League defeat on Thursday by using the corner flag to simulate a gun.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel forward Saied Abu Farchi was sent off for celebrating his goal against Austria in their 3-1 UEFA Nations League defeat on Thursday by using the corner flag to simulate a gun. Abu Farchi headed home in the 55th minute to bring Israel level after Austria had taken the lead through a Romano Schmid penalty before halftime at the Raiffeisen Arena in Linz. The 20-year-old ran to the corner flag, grabbed it and made a gun-firing gesture during his celebration. The referee had booked Abu Farchi four minutes earlier and showed him a second yellow card for the celebration, followed by a red, leaving Israel with 10 players. Austria regained the lead in the 90th minute through Phillipp Mwene, who netted following a cross from Paul Wanner. Sasa Kalajdzic added a third in stoppage time with a close-range finish.

item.title: Cerca de 60 navios passaram pelo Estreito de Ormuz na 4ª, diz autoridade norte-americana
item.description: Cerca de 60 embarcações comerciais atravessaram o Estreito de Ormuz na quarta-feira, transportando o maior volume diário de petróleo bruto desde o início de julho, apesar da guerra em curso entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã, informou uma autoridade norte-americana à Reuters sob condição de anonimato.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cerca de 60 embarcações comerciais atravessaram o Estreito de Ormuz na quarta-feira, transportando o maior volume diário de petróleo bruto desde o início de julho, apesar da guerra em curso entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã, informou uma autoridade norte-americana à Reuters sob condição de anonimato. Aproximadamente 40 desses navios se coordenaram com as Forças Armadas dos EUA para obter proteção, acrescentou a autoridade. Um total quase 22 milhões de barris de petróleo saiu do ponto de estrangulamento marítimo. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente os números apresentados pela autoridade norte-americana. O Estreito de Ormuz tornou-se fundamental para os esforços de encerrar o conflito de quase sete meses entre os EUA e o Irã, com o Irã buscando alívio do bloqueio norte-americano que sufoca sua economia e Washington pressionando Teerã a interromper a interferência na navegação pela importante rota global de abastecimento de petróleo. Antes do início da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, em 28 de fevereiro, o estreito costumava receber cerca de 125 grandes navios comerciais por dia, incluindo petroleiros, navios de gás, graneleiros e embarcações porta-contêineres, representando cerca de 20% do abastecimento diário mundial de petróleo bruto e gás natural liquefeito. A Reuters informou nesta quinta-feira que negociadores dos EUA e do Irã em Nova York avaliam um caminho gradual para sair da guerra, que envolveria a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz por parte de Teerã e a suspensão do bloqueio econômico ao Irã por parte de Washington, segundo fontes próximas às negociações.

item.title: 仏、サウジ西部ヤンブー防衛に部隊派遣 フーシ派攻撃受け＝大統領
item.description: [パリ ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[パリ ２４日 ロイター] - マクロン仏大統領は２４日、エネルギー輸送の要衝であるサウジアラビア西部の紅海沿岸都市ヤンブーを防衛するため、軍部隊のほか、防空システムを派遣すると表明した。

ヤンブーはホルムズ海峡を経由しないサウジ産原油の主要な代替輸出ルートになっているが、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃の標的になっており、原油価格上昇の一因になっている。

マクロン氏は国内テレビのインタビューに対し「ヤンブーを防衛するために兵士、レーダーシステム、防衛システムなどをの軍資源を派遣する。紛争に関与するのではなく、防衛のために派遣する」と述べた。

フーシ派はこの日、サウジの首都リヤドの「重要目標」と、ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設をミサイルと無人機（ドローン）で攻撃したと表明した。

item.title: 米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ５００横ばい、中東協議進展観測で持ち直す
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種がほぼ横ばいで取引を終えた。中東情勢の不透明感から原油価格と...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ５００横ばい、中東協議進展観測で持ち直す 5:25 配信

ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）で15日撮影。REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

［２４日　ロイター］　 - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種がほぼ横ばいで取引を終えた。中東情勢の不透明感から原油価格と米国債利回りが上昇する中、マイクロソフト が軟調な一方、 メタ・プラットフォームズが値上がりした。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合は取引時間中の安値から持ち直した。米国とイランがニューヨークで続けている協議で、イランがホルムズ海峡を開放し米国が対イラン経済封鎖を解除するという、段階的な戦闘終結への道筋が模索されているとロイターが報じたことが背景にある。

原油市場では北海ブレント先物が３％超上昇。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派によるサウジアラビアへのミサイル攻撃を受け、供給混乱への懸念が再燃した。

ＵＳバンク・ウェルス・マネジメントのシニア投資ディレクター、ビル・ノーシー氏は「現在われわれが一つの大きな材料に直面しているという見方を強めるものだ」とし、「原油とインフレ、それが金利に与える影響、さらに金利が資本市場全体に与える影響だ 」と述べた。

ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は２４日、インフレリスクを抑制するために、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が年末までに再び利上げを行う必要があるかもしれないと考えるのは「妥当」だと述べた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種のうち８業種が下落し、素材や主要消費財の下げが目立った。

人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の主要銘柄はまちまちで、マイクロソフトが０．５％安、ブロードコムが１．３％安となる一方、アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（ＡＭＤ）は２．４％上昇した。

メタは４．５％高。同社は前日、新たなＡＩエージェント「ミューズ」 を利用するための小型端末「メタ・チャーム」を発表した。

オラクルは３．５％下落。ニューメキシコ州のデータセンター開発を手がけるブルー・アウル傘下企業に「不可抗力」を通知したと報じられたことが響いた。ブルー・アウルも下落した。

ＭＧＭリゾーツは１１％急落。富豪のバリー・ディラー氏率いる米メディアのピープルが買収計画を撤回したことが響いた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．９対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６８億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１６７億株。
