item.title: Costco tops estimates as discount gas, bulk deals draw inflation-weary shoppers
item.description: Costco Wholesale beat quarterly estimates on Thursday, recording strong comparable sales growth as inflationary pressures drove consumers to its discount gas stations and boosted demand across its warehouses.
item.dc:creator: Angela M, Nicholas Brown
item.content:encoded: Costco Wholesale (COST.O) beat quarterly estimates on Thursday, recording strong comparable sales growth as inflationary pressures drove consumers to its discount gas stations and boosted demand across its warehouses. The warehouse retailer reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $6.60, excluding a one-time 15-cent benefit from tariff refunds, beating analysts' estimates of $6.53, according to LSEG data. Quarterly revenue rose about 11% from a year earlier to $95.72 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $94.86 billion. Total same-store sales excluding gas and foreign exchange effects rose 6.7%, above analysts' expectations of 6.11%. Costco has benefited as consumers look to stretch household budgets, with its low-price bulk model and discounted fuel offering helping attract shoppers amid persistent cost pressures. "It was another well-rounded quarter for Costco, with comparable sales growth continuing to lead its big-box peers, driven by balanced traffic and average ticket growth," CFRA analyst Arun Sundaram said. Gasoline was a key sales driver, with CEO Ron Vachris saying the business had a "record year." Costco gas stations, which usually sell below market value, according to TD Cowen analyst Oliver Chen, have helped pull in price-sensitive customers as the Iran war sends fuel prices soaring. The company received tariff refunds of $184 million during the quarter under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, Costco's CFO Gary Millerchip said in a post-earnings call. The refunds were reinvested through price reductions on some items, including essentials, meat, beverages and some non-food items, CEO Ron Vachris added. The retailer has also seen average basket sizes increase as shoppers consolidate their trips to the store, loading up on groceries and other essentials in one visit rather than doing multiple runs. The company's shares were flat in extended trading. As of Thursday's close, the stock has risen nearly 4% so far this year.

item.title: Oklahoma must allow taxpayer-funded religious charter school, judge rules
item.description: A federal judge in Oklahoma cleared the way on Thursday for a Jewish organization to establish the nation's first taxpayer-funded religious charter school in a case over religious rights in American education that could eventually reach the US Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Oklahoma cleared the way on Thursday for a Jewish organization to establish the nation's first taxpayer-funded religious charter school in a case over religious rights in American education that could eventually reach the US Supreme Court . US District Judge David Russell in Oklahoma City issued a preliminary injunction blocking the state from excluding the National Ben Gamla Jewish Charter School Foundation from Oklahoma's charter program. State law requires charter schools to be nonsectarian. Charter schools are considered public schools under Oklahoma law and draw taxpayer funds from the state government. The judge said the restriction expressly discriminates against otherwise eligible schools solely because of their religious character in violation of the US Constitution's First Amendment protection for the right to exercise one's religion freely without government interference, known as the "free exercise clause." "A long line of Supreme Court precedent supports plaintiffs' position," wrote Russell, an appointee of Republican former President Ronald Reagan. Another provision of the First Amendment, called the "establishment clause," restricts government officials from establishing or endorsing any particular religion or promoting religion over nonreligion. Set up as alternatives to traditional public schools, charter schools typically operate under private management and often feature small class sizes, innovative teaching styles or a particular academic focus. The judge blocked the Republican-led state from enforcing its state law. Several Oklahoma taxpayers and families intervened to defend the law after the Oklahoma Statewide Charter School Board, which had denied Ben Gamla's application, opted not to oppose a ruling against the nonsectarian mandate. Daniel Chen, a lawyer for Ben Gamla at the religious rights legal group Becket, said in a statement that the ruling will ensure it "now gets what it should have had from the start: a fair shot to serve Oklahoma families." "The Constitution doesn't permit the state to welcome every kind of charter school except a religious one," Chen said. Lawyers for the interveners at groups including Americans United for Separation of Church and State and the American Civil Liberties Union in a joint statement said the ruling marked "a dangerous sea change for our democracy." "We will continue to fight for all Oklahomans, who deserve public schools that are secular and open to all students," they said. The ruling came a year after [USN:S0N3RD07K TEXT:"the Supreme Court split 4-4"] on whether to overturn an Oklahoma Supreme Court ruling that had prevented two Catholic dioceses from establishing a taxpayer-funded charter school in the state. The court was unable to resolve the issue after conservative Justice Amy Coney Barrett recused herself from the case. In ruling in favor of Ben Gamla, Russell cited a [USN:LUN2QW019 TEXT:"2022 ruling"] that the Supreme Court delivered that further reduced the separation of church and state by siding with two Christian families who challenged a Maine tuition assistance program that excluded private religious schools. Russell said that, similar to Maine, Oklahoma had by law "created a generally available benefit: the opportunity to apply for and contract with a sponsor to establish a charter school." "But the state categorically excludes religious institutions from participating," the judge wrote.

item.title: BOLSA EUA S&P 500 encerra com queda marginal, enquanto investidores se concentram na guerra entre EUA e Irã
item.description: O S&P 500 fechou com uma queda marginal nesta quinta-feira, com a Microsoft em baixa e a Meta em alta, enquanto a incerteza em relação ao Oriente Médio impulsionou os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: O S&P 500 fechou com uma queda marginal nesta quinta-feira, com a Microsoft em baixa e a Meta em alta, enquanto a incerteza em relação ao Oriente Médio impulsionou os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro. O S&P 500 e o Nasdaq se recuperaram das mínimas do pregão depois que a Reuters noticiou que negociadores dos EUA e do Irã estavam explorando um caminho gradual para sair da guerra, que envolveria a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz por Teerã e o fim do bloqueio econômico imposto por Washington ao Irã. Líderes dos EUA e do Irã trocaram farpas nesta semana na Assembleia Geral da ONU. Os preços do petróleo Brent subiram mais de 3%, para quase US$107 por barril, depois que um ataque com mísseis dos militantes houthis à Arábia Saudita reacendeu os temores de interrupções no abastecimento. “Isso apenas reforça a visão de que estamos lidando com um grande catalisador de mercado neste momento”, disse Bill Northey, diretor sênior de investimentos na U.S. Bank Wealth Management. “Na verdade, tudo gira em torno do petróleo e da inflação e do efeito sobre as taxas de juros, e depois do impacto em cascata dessas taxas nos mercados de capitais.” As gigantes da IA apresentaram resultados mistos: a Microsoft (MSFT.O) caiu 0,5% e a Broadcom (AVGO.O) perdeu 1,3%, enquanto a Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) subiu 2,4%. A Meta (META.O) saltou 4,5%, um dia depois que a empresa de mídia social revelou um pequeno dispositivo portátil para uso com seu assistente de IA recém-lançado. A Oracle (ORCL.N) caiu 3,5% após uma reportagem informar que a empresa enviou uma notificação de “força maior” a um data center no Novo México. As ações da Blue Owl (OWL.N) , desenvolvedora do projeto, também registraram forte queda. Os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiram, com o rendimento do título do Tesouro de 30 anos atingindo seu nível mais alto desde 2004. Rendimentos mais altos tornam os títulos do Tesouro, considerados um porto seguro, relativamente mais atraentes para os investidores do que ações com retornos incertos. O S&P 500 teve variação negativa de 0,02%, encerrando o pregão em 7.704,13 pontos. O Nasdaq oscilou 0,01% para cima, a 26.939,37 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average recuou 0,31%, para 51.349,98 pontos. Oito dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 caíram, liderados pelo setor de materiais (.SPLRCM) , com queda de 1,18%, seguido por uma perda de 0,96% no setor de bens de consumo básico (.SPLRCS) . O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, recebeu o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, na Casa Branca para uma cúpula que deve ter forte caráter simbólico, mas pouca substância em relação a questões como IA, comércio, Taiwan e a guerra no Oriente Médio. Dados divulgados na quarta-feira, sugerindo uma forte atividade empresarial, levaram a um aumento nas expectativas de que o Federal Reserve elevará as taxas de juros novamente, após o aumento de 25 pontos-base na semana passada. Os operadores de mercado estão agora precificando uma chance de quase 70% de um aumento no próximo mês, de acordo com a ferramenta CME FedWatch. O presidente do Fed de Nova York, John Williams, que tem direito a voto no Comitê Federal de Mercado Aberto, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que é razoável supor que o banco central dos EUA possa precisar aumentar as taxas de juros novamente antes do final do ano. A MGM Resorts (MGM.N) despencou 11% depois que a People Inc (PPLI.O) , do magnata da mídia Barry Diller, retirou sua proposta de compra da operadora de cassinos.

item.title: US government seeks to join Elon Musk in challenge against EU's fine on X
item.description: The US government said on Thursday it had formally sought to join a legal challenge filed by billionaire Elon Musk to dismiss a fine of €120 million ($136.51 million) by the European Union against his social media platform X.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The US government said on Thursday it had formally sought to join a legal challenge filed by billionaire Elon Musk to dismiss a fine of €120 million ($136.51 million) by the European Union against his social media platform X. EU tech regulators [USN:L1N3XB0BG TEXT:"fined"] X late last year for breaching online content rules, the first sanction under a landmark legislation that has drawn criticism from Washington. The US Department of Justice said it had filed an application with the EU's General Court in support of X's effort to annul the case. The EU sanction against X followed a two-year-long investigation under the bloc's Digital Services Act (DSA), which requires online platforms to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content. "The European Commission inappropriately attempted to expand its regulatory authority to reach American companies not present or operating within its jurisdiction," Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate of the US Justice Department's civil division said. Europe's crackdown on Big Tech to ensure smaller rivals can compete and consumers have more choice has been criticised by the administration of US President Donald Trump , which alleges it singles out American companies. The European Commission, the EU's executive, has said its laws do not target any nationality and that it is merely defending its digital and democratic standards, which it says serve as the benchmark for the rest of the world. Musk, who has financially backed candidates from Trump's Republican Party in elections and supported Trump himself in the last election, has said the EU's tech regulations stall technological progress. Since Musk's purchase of X, then known as Twitter, in 2022, rights advocates and experts have been widely critical of the platform over what they say is increased hate speech, misinformation and nonconsensual sexually explicit content. ($1 = 0.8790 euros)

item.title: Akamai signs $11.6 billion cloud deal with Anthropic, grants warrant for up to 5% stake
item.description: Akamai Technologies signed an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with Anthropic on Thursday, and issued a warrant that could give the AI lab up to 5% stake in the cloud company, sending its shares surging 22% in extended trading.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: Akamai Technologies (AKAM.O) signed an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with Anthropic on Thursday, and issued a warrant that could give the AI lab up to 5% stake in the cloud company, sending its shares surging 22% in extended trading. The agreement secures a long-term commitment from one of the fastest-growing AI companies, and adds to more than $2.8 billion in multi-year cloud infrastructure deals Akamai announced across its customer base this year. Under the seven-year contract, the warrant would give Anthropic the right to purchase Series B shares at $111.33 each that converts into about 7.7 million shares of Akamai's common stock. [USN:L1N44C004 TEXT:"IPO-bound"] Anthropic has been aggressively expanding its computing power and securing the infrastructure needed to train and run increasingly powerful models, driving multibillion-dollar deals with cloud and data-center providers. It [USN:L4N44N1FK TEXT:"agreed"] to spend $45 billion to rent AI cloud computing power from Nscale's West Virginia data center campus, Reuters reported last month. "Despite growing concerns about potential adverse consequences of agentic AI, infrastructure investment will continue to expand to support increasingly compute-intensive agentic workloads," said Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne. The potential stake "can be seen as a vote of confidence in the durability of AI-driven cloud demand." A portion of the warrant representing about 2% of Akamai's common stock outstanding is tied to Anthropic's $11.6 billion commitment, while the remaining 3% would vest if the companies expand the agreement by up to another $9 billion. Akamai said the total capital expenditure related to the initial commitment is estimated to be about $5.5 billion. The company expects no impact to its annual revenue forecast, and an increase of about $1.7 billion in its 2026 capital spending to secure and pre-purchase components needed to support the agreement, including memory. Separately, Akamai authorized electronics firm Jabil (JBL.N) to purchase about $1.7 billion worth of memory components under an existing services agreement.

item.title: Operações voltam ao normal no porto de Santos após incêndio em equipamento
item.description: As operações no terminal da Neves & Marinheiro, no porto de Santos, foram retomadas após incêndio nesta quinta-feira em um equipamento que transportava trigo, informou a autoridade portuária.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As operações no terminal da Neves & Marinheiro, no porto de Santos, foram retomadas após incêndio nesta quinta-feira em um equipamento que transportava trigo, informou a autoridade portuária. Conforme nota da agência marítima Cargonave, equipes do terminal e de combate a incêndio agiram imediatamente para controlar a situação. O terminal da Neves & Marinheiro fica ao lado de operações da chinesa Cofco, que não foram atingidas, segundo a companhia. A Cofco disse, por meio de sua assessoria de imprensa, que as operações de carregamento no porto seguiram normalmente. Não foi possível falar imediatamente com a Neves & Marinheiro, após várias tentativas pelo telefone.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em queda pressionado por Treasuries e receio fiscal
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quinta-feira, perdendo o patamar dos 184 mil pontos, com o apetite a risco minado por novo avanço nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, além de receios com o cenário fiscal no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quinta-feira, perdendo o patamar dos 184 mil pontos, com o apetite a risco minado por novo avanço nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, além de receios com o cenário fiscal no Brasil. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) caiu 0,99%, a 183.965,91 pontos. Na mínima do dia, chegou a 183.834,97 pontos. Na máxima, subiu a 186.211,43 pontos. O volume financeiro somou R$26,89 bilhões. No exterior, o rendimento do Treasury de 10 anos marcava 5,2209% no final da tarde, de 5,114% na véspera, com preocupações renovadas sobre a inflação e potenciais novos aumentos de juros pelo Federal Reserve. De acordo com a estrategista de ações Rebecca Nossig, da Nomad, o movimento nos juros de longo prazo nos EUA atrai o capital global para a segurança da renda fixa norte-americana, drenando a liquidez e o apetite por ativos de risco em mercados emergentes como o Brasil. Isso, acrescentou, explica a "intensa pressão vendedora sobre a bolsa local e o movimento de realização de lucros". O petróleo referendou os receios sobre a inflação, com o barril sob o contrato Brent fechando o dia com elevação de 3,41%, a US$106,60, diante da ausência de sinais de progressos diplomáticos efetivos nas negociações entre os EUA e o Irã. Em Nova York, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) encerrou quase estável a sessão, que teve ainda como pano de fundo o aguardado encontro entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e seu par chinês, Xi Jinping. Trump afirmou que ele e Xi tiveram uma “ótima reunião”. O analista de renda variável Felipe Cima, da Manchester Investimentos, também destacou como componente negativo o relatório de avaliação fiscal do governo, que indica um gasto acima do esperado e dificuldade maior de conversão das contas, com frustração de receitas. No documento, o governo informou que [USN:L1N45G0HA TEXT:"reduziu"] de R$17,9 bilhões para R$16,1 bilhões a necessidade prevista de contenção total de verbas de ministérios para respeitar regras fiscais, mas apontou significativa piora na previsão de déficit fiscal em 2026. Cima também chamou a atenção para a possível retirada da receita com as bets, além da expectativa de que a sexta-feira possa trazer alguma novidade sobre programa bancado pelo Tesouro Nacional referente ao endividamento das famílias. O mercado fechou com investidores na expectativa de nova pesquisa eleitoral Datafolha nesta quinta-feira. Nos últimos levantamentos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) têm mostrado empate técnico em simulações de segundo turno. Na visão do gestor Luis Stuhlberger, da Verde Asset Management, pode ocorrer uma "[USN:L6N45G112 TEXT:"porrada insana"]" na bolsa se Flávio vencer, mas ele não espera um movimento tão negativo se Lula for reeleito, citando múltiplo perto da média dos governos petistas passados e baixa exposição de investidores a ações. Mas, embora considere um alívio uma eventual troca no Planalto, criticando principalmente a política fiscal de Lula, e estime uma euforia de curto prazo no caso de eventual vitória de Flávio, ele citou que o candidato do PL "não tem um projeto de governo". "Acho que o Brasil vai ser aquele negócio: não se encante com excesso de otimismo", afirmou em evento em São Paulo.

item.title: India's Akasa in talks with Boeing to order 200 737 MAX aircraft, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: India's third-largest airline, Akasa Air, is in talks to order more than 200 Boeing 737 MAX jets, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's third-largest airline, Akasa Air, is in talks to order more than 200 Boeing (BA.N) 737 MAX jets, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. A decision on the order is expected early next year, with terms likely finalized in the second half of 2027, the report said, adding that the purchase would support Akasa's fleet growth beyond 2032. Akasa Air and Boeing did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. The report comes as the Mumbai-based budget carrier expands its fleet of Boeing's [USN:L3N3FY1XA TEXT:"fuel-efficient jets"]. The airline, which began operations in 2022, operates 43 Boeing 737 MAX jets and has orders for 226 more aircraft for delivery over the next decade. Akasa is targeting a [USN:L1N42V063 TEXT:"30% capacity"] increase by March 2027 and is weighing participation in the government's emergency credit guarantee scheme, its finance chief said in June.

France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route, Macron says

PARIS, Sept 24 (Reuters) – France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday.

Macron also said a US ban on diesel exports, which the White House has denied is under consideration, would be “catastrophic,” both globally and for the US economy.

Macron was speaking in a wide-ranging primetime television interview on the international situation, in which he also warned about possible Russian attacks on French soil.

Show Full Article

Facing growing pressure at home over high energy prices, Macron sought to assure the French that France had adequate gas and oil supplies as winter approaches. He said Paris was actively working to ensure flows were not disrupted.

Crude oil prices have surged recently as the main alternative route for Saudi oil exports through Yanbu has come under missile attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

“We are going to send military resources, that is to say, soldiers, radar systems and defence systems, to protect this site – not to get us involved in any conflicts, but to protect this site,” Macron told TF1 and France 2 TV.

RUSSIAN THREAT

Macron dismissed a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the US Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments about the threat of potential drone attacks from the Mediterranean.

“I can deny it. The CIA did not inform French services,” he said.

Still, Macron said Russia is multiplying hostile and criminal acts against European countries, and France could face strikes similar to the failed attack in Leipzig. Germany said Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack in August on the Leipzig airport.

Macron gathered French party chiefs at the Elysee last week to brief them on the growing threat from Russia. He later said he had ordered his government to draw up a plan to protect critical infrastructure against drone and cyber attacks.

Macron said Moscow was seeking to intimidate Europe and break the continent’s resolve in supporting Ukraine.

Russia says European allegations of hybrid attacks are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.

Yet Macron’s position on Russia was weakened this week after France shocked other EU members by getting Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Alisher Usmanov exempted from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. That prompted Azerbaijan to pardon a French national jailed for espionage.

(Reporting by Dominique Vidalon, Inti Landauro, Leigh Thomas and Gabriel Stargardter; Editing by Cynthia Osterman)

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、対円で158円後半 ＦＲＢ当局者タカ派発言で追加利上げ観測
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２４日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し上昇し、対円では一...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、対円で158円後半　ＦＲＢ当局者タカ派発言で追加利上げ観測 4:53 配信

２００９年１１月撮影　REUTERS/Yuriko Nakao

［ニューヨーク　２４日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し上昇し、対円では一時９月２日以来のドル高／円安水準となる１５８．９８円を付けた。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者によるタカ派的な発言を受けて追加利上げ観測が強まったことに加え、堅調な米経済成長への期待を背景に米国債利回りの上昇が続いていることでドル買いが進んでいる。

終盤の取引でドル／円は０．３２％高の１５８．８２円。 片山さつき財務相はこの日、７月の日米協調為替介入を支えた基本原則はなお維持されているとの認識を示したものの、先週の日銀利上げを受けても金融引き締めペースの加速につながるとの見方は広がらず、市場心理は引き続き不安定な状態にある。

日銀は１７─１８日の金融政策決定会合で政策金利を１．２５％に引き上げたものの直後に円安が進み、関係筋によると日銀は１８日、為替介入の準備段階とされる「レートチェック」に踏み切っていた。

米国では企業活動の拡大と物価圧力の高まりを示す経済指標を受け、この日も国債利回りが上昇。３０年債利回りは２００４年６月以来、１０年債利回りは約２０年ぶりの高水準を付けた。この日は、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派によるサウジアラビアに対するミサイル攻撃を受け原油価格が再び上昇。インフレ懸念の高まりにつながっている。

ＦＲＢは１５─１６日に開いた連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定。利上げは２０２３年７月以来３年２カ月ぶりで、ＦＯＭＣに合わせて公表された金利・経済見通しでは年内に少なくともあと１回の利上げ実施が示唆された。

ＦＯＭＣ後、複数のＦＲＢ当局者がインフレ鈍化が進まなければ追加利上げの可能性があるとの認識を表明。この日はフィラデルフィア地区連銀のポールソン総裁がインフレ率をＦＲＢが目標とする２％に戻すには追加利上げが必要になる可能性があるとの見方を示したほか、クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁はインフレ圧力はなお高く、この状況が長引けばインフレ率を目標水準に押し下げることが難しくなると述べた。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、ＦＲＢが１０月２７─２８日の次回ＦＯＭＣで少なくとも０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定する確率は６８．６％。１週間前の５５．４％から上昇した。

ＦＸストリート（ニューヨーク）のシニアアナリスト、ジョセフ・トレビサーニ氏は「２年債利回りは２００８年の金融危機以降のレンジ上限にあり、３０年債利回りは２２年ぶりの高水準、１０年債利回りも１９年ぶりの高水準にある。外為市場参加者にとっては、これ以上の説明は必要ないだろう」とし、「ＦＲＢは今回の原油高は供給ショックによるものと理解しており、その影響をある程度見極めようとしている。ＦＲＢは第３・四半期の経済成長見通しに注目している」と述べた。

終盤の取引で主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．１５％高の１０１．２８。上昇は４営業日連続で、一時は１０１．３９と、７月２９日以来の高水準を付けた。

ユーロ／ドルは０．０７％安の１．１３７２ドル。一時は１．１３５８ドルに下落し、７月２８日以来の安値を更新した。

ドルはスイスフランに対し０．３４％高の０．８２８スイスフラン。一時は０．８２９６スイスフランに上昇し、２０２５年５月以来の高水準を付けた。スイス国立銀行（中央銀行）はこの日、予想通り政策金利を０％に据え置いた。足元でスイスフランが軟化する中、為替市場への介入は「必要に応じて」行うとし、従来より姿勢を軟化させた。

ドル／円　ＮＹ終値 158.83/158.88

始値 158.74

高値 159.03

安値 158.61

ユーロ／ドル　ＮＹ終値 1.1379/1.1382

始値 1.1373

高値 1.1391

安値 1.1360

item.title: 米30年債利回りが5.45%超え、20年超ぶり高水準 インフレ懸念で
item.description:
Amanda Cooper Sophie Kiderlin
[ロンドン ２４日 ロイター] - 米３０年債利回りが２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米30年債利回りが5.45%超え、20年超ぶり高水準　インフレ懸念で 4:36 配信

米国財務省入口。２月撮影。REUTERS/Ken Cedeno

Amanda Cooper　Sophie Kiderlin

[ロンドン　２４日　ロイター] - 米３０年債利回りが２４日、一時５．４５％をわずかに上回る水準まで上昇し、２００４年以来、２０年超ぶりの高水準を付けた。堅調な経済成長や高水準の債務、インフレ懸念を一段と強めるエネルギー価格の上昇を背景に、投資家が国債保有に対しより高い利回りを求める中、売りが拡大している。

指標となる１０年債利回りは５．１５８％となっている。

米国の３０年固定住宅ローン金利は戦争前と比べ１％ポイント上昇し、足元では７％と過去約２年間で最も高い水準にある。住宅ローン金利は米国債利回りに連動する。

イラン戦争によるエネルギー価格の高騰や、政府支出を巡る懸念が強まる中、債券市場は数カ月にわたって圧力にさらされており、利回りは数十年ぶりの高水準に達している。

大和キャピタル・マーケッツの経済調査責任者、クリス・シクルナ氏は「金利が上昇するほど全体の見通しが悪化するのは明らかだ。米国の住宅ローン金利はより高くなり、連邦政府の債務利払い負担も一層大きくなる」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：世界のディーゼル価格が過去最高、主要生産国の輸出急減　一段高も 焦点：トランプ氏の金利1％論、政権周辺でも異論　物価高批判そらす狙いか アングル：ＮＡＴＯが問われる「次の戦争」への備え、ドローン時代の適応に課題 アングル：「チャイナプラスワン」に逆流の兆し、中国回帰を選ぶメーカーの事情 コラム：何が豪ドルを動かしているのか＝高島修氏 最終更新: 9/25(金) 4:36 ロイター

item.title: ＵＡＥとオマーンがイラン航空便停止、米制裁受け
item.description:
Federico Maccioni Eman Abouhassira Timour Azhari
[ドバイ／リヤド ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Federico Maccioni　Eman Abouhassira　Timour Azhari

[ドバイ／リヤド ２４日 ロイター] - アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）やオマーンを含むイラン周辺国は２４日、イラン航空会社の運航を停止した。イランとの取引がある第三国の企業を標的にするという米国の政策転換の影響が表面化した形だ。

中東最大の航空ハブであるＵＡＥの民間航空総局は、米国の新たな政策を受け、追って通知するまでイラン航空会社の全便を停止すると発表した。

イランの半国営タスニム通信によると、オマーンやジョージア、アゼルバイジャン、およびイラク首都バグダッドへの便も停止された。当局は、シーア派イスラム教徒の主要な巡礼地であるイラクのナジャフの別の空港に便を振り替える方向で調整していると伝えた。

湾岸地域の他の国もイラン便を制限したもようだ。

イランは、米国が主導する空の封鎖の履行が、緊張激化につながる恐れがあると示唆してきた。２３日には、イラン国家安全保障最高評議会のモフセン・レザイ書記が、周辺国が米国に協力してイラン便の運航を停止させれば、イランはそれらの国の空港が機能しないようにすると述べた。

item.title: ネタニヤフ氏、国連演説でイスラエル擁護 退席者やＮＹ市長を非難
item.description: [国連 ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連 ２４日 ロイター] - イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相は２４日、国連総会の一般討論演説で、中東地域における自国の行動を擁護した。総選挙を前に、深まる国際的孤立に対抗する狙いだったが、演説が始まると多数の外交官や各国代表が抗議の意思を示して退席した。

ネタニヤフ氏はパレスチナ自治区ガザでの戦闘を巡り国外で批判の高まりに直面する一方、国内では１０月２７日の総選挙での再選に向けて選挙戦を展開している。

同氏は退席した代表らを「道徳的な臆病者」と非難し、「イスラエルは、まさにこの場を去った国々の多くを守っている」と主張した。

また、自身を「戦争犯罪者」と呼んだニューヨーク市のマムダニ市長を非難し、パレスチナのイスラム組織ハマスの戦闘員を支援していると主張。さらに、欧州の指導者らが「反ユダヤ主義の暴徒」に屈したと批判したほか、カタールとトルコがイスラエルに関する虚偽の情報を広めていると非難した。

マムダニ氏については、「私がここに来るのを止めようとした。私を黙らせようとした。しかし、私を黙らせることはできない。真実を黙らせることはできない」とし、「単純な真実がある。イスラエルはジェノサイド（集団虐殺）を行っていない。イスラエルはジェノサイドを防いだのだ」と主張した。

さらに、「わが国と勇敢な兵士たちについてうそを広めている者たち、この議場にいる者であれ、反ユダヤ主義的なニューヨーク市長の事務所にいる者であれ、私はこう言いたい。恥を知れ」と述べた。

マムダニ氏は市長選で、ネタニヤフ氏がニューヨークを訪問すれば戦争犯罪の疑いで逮捕すると公約したが、後に法的権限がないと判断したと表明していた。

マムダニ氏は声明で「ネタニヤフ首相はこれまでと同様、パレスチナ人へのジェノサイドを取り繕うことを目的とした根拠のないうそを繰り返すために演説を利用した」と反論。「どんなうそをもってしても、同氏が戦争犯罪と人道に対する罪の疑いで国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）の逮捕状の対象であり続けている事実は変えられない」と述べた。

ネタニヤフ氏の苦戦が予想されるイスラエル総選挙まで５週間を切る中、演説は約４０分に及び、選挙運動を思わせる内容となった。

今回の訪米でトランプ大統領との首脳会談は予定されていないが、演説ではトランプ氏を称賛。「われわれは国家防衛を続ける。われわれは勝ち続ける。ほかに選択肢はない。野蛮な者たちとのこの戦いにおいて、トランプ大統領以上のパートナーはいない」とし、「その大胆な指導力に感謝する」と述べた。

こうした中、ニューヨークの国連本部周辺には数百人の抗議者が集まり、「イスラエルへの武器供与をやめろ」などと叫んだほか、道路を封鎖するなどして警察に拘束された。

item.title: ホルムズ海峡通過船、23日は約60隻に急増＝米当局者
item.description: [ワシントン ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２４日　ロイター] - 米国とイランの戦争が続く中、２３日に約６０隻の商業船がホルムズ海峡を通過し、前日２２日の３隻から大幅に増加したことが分かった。また、原油の１日当たり輸送量は７月上旬以降で最大となった。米当局者がロイターに匿名を条件に明らかにした。

同当局者によると、２３日に通過した約６０隻のうち、約４０隻は米軍と連携して護衛を受けていたという。ホルムズ海峡を通過した原油は合計で約２２００万バレルに上った。

ロイターは、同当局者が示した数値を独自に確認することはできなかった。

海運データ（速報値）によると、前日２２日にホルムズ海峡を通過したコモディティー（商品）輸送船はわずか３隻と、前日の４隻から減少し、１０日移動平均の約１５隻を下回っていた。

ロイターは２４日、関係筋の話として、米国とイランがニューヨークで続けている協議で、イランがホルムズ海峡を開放し、米国が対イラン経済封鎖を解除するという、段階的な戦闘終結への道筋が模索されていると報じた。

item.title: Nyrstar launches strategic review of Dutch zinc smelting operations
item.description: Nyrstar, owned by commodities group Trafigura, has launched a strategic review of its loss-making Budel zinc smelting operations in the Netherlands due to r
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Nyrstar, owned by commodities group Trafigura, has launched a strategic review of its loss-making Budel zinc smelting operations in the Netherlands due to rising energy costs and government policies, it said on Thursday. Operations to produce the metal mainly used to galvanise steel will continue as normal during the review, which is expected to conclude by the end of 2026, Nyrstar added in a statement. “Nyrstar Budel faces significant pressure in terms of tough market conditions, elevated energy prices and historically low treatment and refining charges over a sustained period,” said CEO Guido Janssen. “The operation is losing money every year and the conditions for next year look particularly difficult, given rising energy costs, together with a lack of supportive government policy.” Adding to the pressure was a decision by the Dutch government not to include provisions for grid cost mitigation for energy-intensive industries in its 2027 budget, Nyrstar said. The Budel smelter, with a capacity to produce 315,000 metric tons per year of zinc, was suspended in the second half of January 2024 due to high energy costs and restarted in May of that year. “This is a significant decision point for Budel. The review will allow us to carefully assess the site’s position and the options available, while continuing to consider whether concrete action can materially improve the business case,” Janssen said. (Reporting by Eric Onstad; Editing by Susan Fenton)

item.title: MercadoLibre launches deliveries within an hour, expands pharmacy business in Brazil
item.description: Adds details in bullets 1-3 SAO PAULO, Sept 24 (Reuters) - MercadoLibre MELI.O launched product deliveries within an hour in Brazil, starting in the city of
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Adds details in bullets 1-3 SAO PAULO, Sept 24 (Reuters) - MercadoLibre MELI.O launched product deliveries within an hour in Brazil, starting in the city of Sao Paulo, Fernando Yunes, the firm's executive vice president of commerce, said on Thursday. The Latin American e-commerce and fintech company also will expand its pharmacy business in the country, with its own pharmacy in Sao Paulo beginning to sell prescription products this month, Yunes said at a company event. MercadoLibre will add third-party pharmacies to its e-commerce platform in Brazil as of October, kicking off in Sao Paulo with three drugstore chains, which were not named. The company expects to have 20 third-party physical drugstore locations in Sao Paulo on its platform by the end of the year. The one-hour service, which started as a test in an undisclosed region of Sao Paulo and is expected to be expanded, will include products such as medications, food and others. (Reporting by Andre Romani; Editing by Chris Reese and Cynthia Osterman) ((fernando.cardoso@thomsonreuters.com;))

item.title: Trump-Xi summit in Washington begins with great fanfare but low expectations
item.description: “We had a great meeting,” US President Donald Trump said after a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, earlier hailing a “truly great friendship” with the Chinese leader.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump-Xi summit in Washington begins with great fanfare but low expectations

“We had a great meeting,” US President Donald Trump said after a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, earlier hailing a “truly great friendship” with the Chinese leader.

US President Donald Trump, right, China's President Xi Jinping watch a silent drill platoon review on the new helipad from the Blue Room Balcony of the White House, Thursday, Sep 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: AP/Alex Brandon)

25 Sep 2026 03:04AM (Updated: 25 Sep 2026 06:39AM)

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday (Sep 24) for a lavish state summit expected to be heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with both leaders keen to showcase stable ties despite a host of thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran. The subject of Taiwan, perhaps the most difficult, came up during a bilateral meeting in which Xi urged the US to oppose "Taiwan independence", according to a readout from the official Chinese news agency Xinhua shortly after it concluded.  The White House did not immediately provide its own readout of the discussion. Xi had been expected to press Trump this week to halt arms sales to Taiwan. Following his visit to China in May, Trump said he was holding in abeyance an arms package to Taiwan worth some US$14 billion and called it a "very good negotiating chip".

The move left some US allies in Asia and even some of Trump's fellow Republicans concerned that he may be tempted to soften Washington's support for Taipei in exchange for economic wins with China.  China has long asserted territorial ownership of Taiwan, a democratically governed island that relies on US power to counter Beijing's threats.  Despite backing Taiwan, the US has traditionally avoided taking an official stance on the island's independence.

US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping walk back to the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Sep 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Evan Vucci)

Earlier on Thursday at the White House , Trump touted his "truly great friendship" with Xi and said the two powers had made strides on trade since his trip to China in May . "During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and 'super intelligence'," Trump said, using his alternative name for artificial intelligence .  "The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come." Speaking after Trump, Xi said the competition between the US and China should be a "healthy one".  US companies were welcome in China, he said, adding that he hopes "Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States". Xi also said both militaries should maintain regular dialogue to improve crisis prevention. "The Thucydides trap can be overcome," he said, referring to the academic theory that sees a risk of rivalry between a rising and an established power spiralling into open conflict. The summit, Xi's first visit to Washington in more than a decade, is the second meeting this year between the leaders of the world's two biggest economies.

US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping walk along the Colonnade of the White House, on Sep 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: AP/Jacquelyn Martin)

POMP AND CIRCUMSTANCE For Trump, who relishes ceremony and prizes his ties with powerful leaders, the visit is as much a matter of national prestige as an opportunity for high-stakes diplomacy.  The US president aimed to reciprocate the grand welcome he received in China in May. But Trump and Xi's remarks were not carried live by any US television networks, which have collectively declined to provide footage in protest of the White House's ban of CNN, MS Now and Politico . Trump greeted Xi on arrival on Wednesday evening with a red carpet on the tarmac, the first time a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews since President Barack Obama met Pope Francis in 2015, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events. Following their remarks on Thursday, the two leaders observed a military ceremony including a flyover at the Rose Garden, with Chinese flags waving from the Oval Office roof alongside US flags, before a scheduled bilateral meeting. Trump's embrace of Xi could complicate his campaign message at home ahead of November's midterm elections, when Republicans' narrow congressional majorities are at stake as voters fret about inflation and the war on Iran. The president for months has labelled Democrats "communists" in an effort to paint them as too extreme, but he welcomed Xi, the head of the Chinese Communist Party, on Thursday as a dear personal friend.

US President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and his wife, Peng Liyuan, attend a ceremony near the colonnade in the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Sep 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Jonathan Ernst)

US President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, his wife, Peng Liyuan, and other officials attend a ceremony near the colonnade in the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Sep 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Jonathan Ernst)

BREAKTHROUGHS UNLIKELY Despite the fanfare, analysts say major breakthroughs are unlikely, with tangible outcomes potentially limited to an extension of a trade truce expiring in November and an agreement to examine threats posed by artificial intelligence. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that they had agreed to extend until Jan 10 an agreement that paused a trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100 per cent. Trump wrote in a Truth Social post on Thursday morning that the two leaders would discuss "super intelligence" but again indicated he has little interest in imposing new regulations, despite concerns from industry leaders that AI could eventually pose a threat to humans. "Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is," Trump wrote. "That is China's position also." During his comments on Thursday, Xi said both countries have "the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control." Analysts say intense competition between the two powers in AI is likely to limit the scope for anything beyond symbolic agreements.

Related:

Highlights: Trump hails 'tremendous strides' and Xi calls for 'healthy' competition as leaders meet

Trump’s high-level welcome for Xi puts personal diplomacy in focus, analysts say

KEEPING TIES STABLE People familiar with the plans say the talks could also yield deals to lower some tariffs, combat drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue, while Trump is expected to seek the release of Americans and others detained in China. Xi appears to be in a stronger position, having overseen a surge in China's trade and firmly in control of supplies of rare earth minerals that give him powerful leverage. Both leaders see advantages in keeping relations stable, with Trump mired in the unpopular Iran war and Xi grappling with domestic economic challenges. But beneath the surface are challenges that could reignite tensions, including disputes over Taiwan, export controls and AI. The leaders will likely discuss the Iran war, but there has been little sign Beijing is willing to exert pressure on its ally to yield to US demands. The guest list for Thursday's state dinne r includes CEOs like Apple's Tim Cook, Amazon's Jeff Bezos, Alphabet's Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Tesla's Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, but despite such an array, people familiar with US plans say Trump is likely to maintain firm export controls on US tech Xi wants loosened.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: 米イラン、段階的停戦案を模索 ホルムズ海峡開放と封鎖解除が軸＝関係筋
item.description:
Samia Nakhoul Parisa Hafezi John Irish
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Samia Nakhoul　Parisa Hafezi　John Irish

[２４日 ロイター] - 米国とイランがニューヨークで続けている協議で、イランがホルムズ海峡を開放し、米国が対イラン経済封鎖を解除するという、段階的な戦闘終結への道筋が模索されていることが複数の関係筋の話で分かった。

原油輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡は、開始から約７カ月が経過した米イラン紛争の終結に向けた交渉の中心的な争点になっている。

イラン関係筋２人、中東地域の当局者２人、西側外交筋２人がロイターに明らかにしたところによると、イランも米国も交渉上の切り札を先に手放すことを望んでいないため、協議は大きな障害に直面している。ただ、イランは対立の長期化がもたらす経済的代償も認識しているという。

イラン高官は、行き詰まりを打開する最も現実的な方法は段階的な取り決めになると指摘。イランがホルムズ海峡での航行を認める見返りとして、米国が経済封鎖を解除し、イランが凍結資産へのアクセスを回復する可能性もあるという。この高官は国連総会の会場で「危機を段階的に解決することが前進への道になり得る。まず封鎖を終わらせ、ホルムズ海峡を開放することだ」と述べた。

こうした案を実現させるには、７月に崩壊した従来の合意に続く新たな暫定的な取り決めをトランプ米大統領が受け入れる必要がある。

トランプ大統領は、１１月３日の中間選挙後に米国とイランが合意に達する可能性があるとの見方を示しているが、欧州の高官はイランには「非常に長い要求リスト」があると指摘した。

米ホワイトハウス当局者は「イランは合意を切望しているが、トランプ大統領が主導権を握っており、米国にとって最善の決定を下す」とした上で、トランプ氏は「適切な条件の下」でイランとの対話には前向きだが、交渉を急ぐ必要はないとの考えを示していると語った。また、米国はホルムズ海峡を掌握しており、イラン経済が「崩壊しつつある」ことから「非常に強い立場」にあると強調し、トランプ氏はイランに「翻弄される」よりも、「不可避のイラン崩壊」が進むに任せることに満足していると語った。

米国の元イラン交渉担当者デニス・ロス氏は、中間選挙前に合意が成立する可能性は３０％にとどまるとの見方を示した。ただ、双方とも選挙後よりも選挙前に合意する強い理由があるかもしれないとも指摘し、「イランを真に締め付けているのは封鎖だ。息の根を止めつつある」と述べた。

イラン高官は、外交による打開策を模索する一方で、イランは米国との戦闘再開の可能性にも備えていると述べ、米国が経済封鎖と武力の脅しを威圧の手段として用いていると非難。「われわれの指は引き金にかかっている。米国は何をすべきか分かっているが、彼らの過大な要求のせいで、外交でこの問題を解決できる可能性は極めて低い」と語った。

中東地域の関係筋によると、封鎖の終結がより喫緊の優先課題になる中、イランはホルムズ海峡の通航料徴収の要求を主要な合意文書から外し、代わりに付属文書に盛り込むことに前向きになっている。ただ、いかなる取り決めも一時的なものにとどまり、イランの要求を正式に放棄するものではないという。

「イランが主に重視しているのはホルムズ海峡での通航料の徴収ではなく、この水路に対する行政的な管理権の維持だ。イランは通航料の問題を先送りする用意はあるかもしれないが、海峡の行政的管理権を手放すことはないだろう」と述べた。

＜終わりなき紛争への懸念＞

湾岸諸国の首脳はニューヨークでトランプ氏と会談した際、イランが交渉復帰を拒否した場合に米国が軍事行動を再開するかどうかを含め、中間選挙後の米国の最終目標について説明を求めた。

中東関係筋によると、首脳らはイランによるホルムズ海峡の支配をいかなる形でも認めないという共通の立場を伝え、航行の自由が回復されるべきであり、この戦略的水路が湾岸諸国への威圧の手段になってはならないと訴えた。一方で、米・イラン間のさらなる紛争に関与しないという地域の決意を反映し、緊張緩和と政治プロセスも強く求めたという。

アブダビを拠点とするシンクタンク、エミレーツ政策センターのエブテサム・アルケトビ所長は「トランプ氏の最終目標が何なのか、圧力路線に代わる選択肢が何なのか、依然として不明だ」と指摘。「対照的にイラン側は自らが何を望んでいるかを分かっている。彼らは明確な目的を持ってホルムズ海峡とバベルマンデブ海峡を通じて地域情勢を作り替えようとしているが、米政府はまだ道筋を定めていない」と述べた。

協議に詳しい西側当局者は「全てはホルムズ海峡の開放に尽きる。われわれは皆、国内で圧力にさらされており、イランもそれを分かっている」と語った。

item.title: Yalcouye makes dream debut as Ivory Coast beat Ghana in heavyweight clash
item.description: Ivory Coast debutant Malick Yalcouye scored the first goal and won the penalty for the second as they beat neighbours Ghana 2-0 in a fiery start to Africa Cup of Nations qualifying on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Ivory Coast debutant Malick Yalcouye scored the first goal and won the penalty for the second as they beat neighbours Ghana 2-0 in a fiery start to Africa Cup of Nations qualifying on Thursday. Captain Frank Kessie converted a 58th-minute penalty in Bouake but it was the 20-year-old Brighton & Hove Albion attacker who stole the show in his first appearance, handing the home side the lead with a powerful left footed strike from outside the penalty area one minute before halftime. Both the Ivorians and Ghanaians had got to the last-32 at the World Cup in mid-year and were playing their first game since their exploits at the tournament in Canada, Mexico and the US. The Group C encounter was the first game back in charge for coach Herve Renard, who won the Cup of Nations with Ivory Coast in 2015, and whose new-look team dominated proceedings against a Ghana side hit by injury and missing the likes of Mohamed Kudus and Antoine Semenyo. The opening day of the group qualifiers for next year’s finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda also had wins for Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mauritania, Namibia and Zimbabwe. However, Tunisia, who were the only one of 10 African teams not to advance past the first phase of the World Cup, let an early lead slip and were held 1-1 at home by Uganda as their disappointing form continued. DR Congo won 2-0 at home in Kinshasa against Equatorial Guinea with Chancel Mbemba heading in early and Yoane Wissa adding the second while also in Group E, Zimbabwe fought back from 2-0 down at halftime to beat Sierra Leone 3-2 with Marshall Munetsi (2) and Tawanda Chirewa scoring. LATE INSURANCE GOAL Cameroon debutant David Nyengue opened the scoring and Bryan Mbeumo added the second in Garoua but they had to sweat it out for a 3-1 triumph after tiny Comoros pulled one back through Bundesliga-based Warmed Omari. Cameroon got a late insurance goal from English-born Daniel Namasso. Libya netted a last-gasp penalty to salvage a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana behind closed doors in Tripoli, where there was a stadium ban because of previous supporter violence. Botswana striker Tumisang Orebonye scored a double in the first half to put his side on course for a rare away win before Maruwan Alhibeeshi thrashed home from the edge of the area to pull one back in the 87th minute. Botswana substitute Mothusi Cooper gave away a stoppage-time penalty with a clumsy challenge, allowing Ezoo El Mariamy to rescue a draw. Mauritania won 3-1 over the Central African Republic in Casablanca, Morocco, which included a superb chipped effort over the goalkeeper from Dawda Camara, while Betuel Muzeu scored the only goal as Namibia edged Congo.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（24日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
続落して取引を終えた。原油先物価格の上昇を受けて、インフレ懸念が高まった。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は３...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（24日） 3:37 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。原油先物価格の上昇を受けて、インフレ懸念が高まった。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は３日連続で下落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．８５％安だった。

米・イランの戦闘終結に向けた協議に大きな進展の兆しが見られない中、原油価格が上昇。英１０年債利回りは一時５．３８％を付けた。

石油大手のＢＰは２．６％、シェルは１．７％それぞれ上昇した。

一方、エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは１．３％、防衛大手ＢＡＥシステムズは１．５％、いずれも下落。利益見通しを下方修正した住宅建設のビストリー・グループは３．１％値下がりした。保険のスタンダード・ライフは４．２％、テクノロジー・サービスプロバイダーのコンピュータセンターは４．４％、それぞれ下落した。

イングランド銀行（英中銀）の副総裁２人は今後の利上げの可能性を示唆。金融政策委員会の１人の委員はインフレリスクを判断する上で冬場の動向が鍵になるとの見方を示した。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。原油価格の上昇を受けてユーロ圏の債券利回りが高水準で推移し、投資家にリスクを回避する姿勢が強まった。主要な地域指数も大半がマイナス圏だった。

米イランの交渉に進展の兆しが見られず、ブレント原油先物価格は１バレル＝１００ドルを上回る水準で取引された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は１．６０％、工業株指数は１．４２％、ヘルスケア株指数は０．１４％、いずれも下落した。

直近の四半期決算を発表したスウェーデンのファストファッション大手Ｈ＆Ｍは２．０％安だった。

一方、石油・ガス株指数は１．１２％高。食品・飲料株指数は０．７０％、個人・家庭用品株指数は０．２１％それぞれ上昇した。

米中首脳会談に関心が集まる中、ベセント米財務長官は２３日、米中が「貿易休戦」の延長で合意したと明らかにした。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが上昇した。原油価格の再上昇に加え、堅調な企業活動指標を受けて欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）による追加金融引き締めの観測が強まった。

ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ１０年債利回りは１７年超ぶりの高水準となる３．５７９８％まで上昇。終盤では３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇となった。

堅調な経済指標も債券売りに拍車をかけた。独ＩＦＯ経済研究所が２４日発表した９月の業況指数は８９．９と、前月の８８．８から上昇し、市場予想を上回った。nL6N45G0JX

短期金融市場の先物は、ＥＣＢが年末までに約３５ｂｐの引き締めを行うことを織り込んでおり、これは０．２５％ポイントの利上げ１回と、２回目の利上げ確率が約４０％であることを意味する。先物は今後１２カ月間に０．２５％ポイントの利上げが４回行われることを織り込んでいる。

ドイツ２年債利回りは横ばいの３．２８４％。

フランス１０年債利回りは一時、１８年超ぶりの高水準となる４．６９６％まで上昇した。

仏独１０年債の利回り格差は１１１ｂｐ超まで拡大し、２０１２年半ば以来の最大幅となった。スプレッドの拡大は一般に、投資家がドイツ国債と比較してフランス国債保有のリスクが高まっていると認識している兆候と見なされる。

item.title: White House reinstates access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico following judge's order
item.description: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump's ban of the three news outlets likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey, Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump 's [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"ban of the three news outlets"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored. The midday reinstatement came after a chaotic few hours earlier on Thursday when the journalists continued to be blocked from entering the White House grounds. That prompted the three news organizations to request an immediate hearing before US District Judge Tim Kelly, who issued his decision overnight. Kelly, acting in a lawsuit brought by CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday, ordered a halt to Trump's ban for 14 days in a press freedom case that has played out over the past week in the courtroom and White House grounds. Kelly found that the revocation of the White House credentials of the journalists "likely violated their constitutional due process rights." The judge, who Trump appointed in 2017 during his first presidential term, also raised doubts about the US Justice Department's national security arguments for justifying the ban, noting that Trump himself had said the action was due to what the president alleged was false or negative coverage. Hours after Kelly issued his order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico told the judge they remained barred, and asked for the emergency hearing. Politico said its reporter's credentials were confiscated. An MS NOW reporter said she was blocked from the White House. CNN said some of its staff members were denied entry onto the grounds. In response, Micah Stopperich, the director of press operations at the White House, said in a court filing that the White House began the process of reinstating press badges for affected reporters at 7:25 a.m., and that the "White House press team dropped badges at the entry gate for members of the press to pick up around 9:55 a.m." After receiving Stopperich's declaration, the judge denied the request by the news organizations for an emergency hearing but gave them an opportunity to inform him of any factual developments later in the day. The sharpest conflict yet between Trump and the press played out during a key diplomatic moment for the US president: his appearance at the United Nations General Assembly in New York and his hosting of Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. A source familiar with the White House television press pool said its members would not reinstate their coverage until the White House formally reinstates CNN to the pool. Earlier this week, they had suspended pooled coverage in solidarity with CNN. There were no TV pool cameras set up for Xi's arrival on the White House's South Lawn on Thursday morning, and FOX News, MS NOW and CNN did not air the two leaders' arrival ceremony live. During Trump's welcome of Xi to the White House, the president made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about the Chinese having the friendliest press corps. CNN is one of the five news organizations – along with ABC, CBS, FOX News and NBC – that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organizing coverage and provide footage to other outlets. CNN had been scheduled to cover Trump's trip to New York for the General Assembly on Monday, but was not able to provide a pool feed. NATIONAL SECURITY CONCERNS Trump announced the ban on Friday on his social media platform, saying those news organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." Trump framed their reporting as a threat to US national security. The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets. Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and stop enforcing the ban for two weeks. The judge rejected the administration's stated national security concerns. "The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," Kelly wrote. In a filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department accused the outlets of threatening national security with their coverage, citing stories about US missile stockpiles, construction of Trump's White House ballroom and turnout at the recent Republican midterm convention. Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the three outlets, welcomed the judge's decision in a statement, saying: "This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court's swift action." TENSIONS WITH THE PRESS Although other presidential administrations have battled with the press, Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. Upending decades of tradition, his White House had denied basic access to many major news organizations, launched personal attacks on journalists and filed multiple lawsuits against news organizations. Kelly's ruling came a day after Trump experienced another legal setback. On Wednesday, an Iowa judge [USN:L4N45F1L5 TEXT:"dismissed"] Trump's 2024 lawsuit against the Des Moines Register newspaper and pollster J. Ann Selzer. Trump sued the Register, its parent company Gannett and Selzer over a poll published ahead of the November 2024 US election that showed Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris leading him in Iowa. Trump accused the newspaper and its longtime pollster of fraudulently misleading readers. In his ruling Wednesday, Iowa District Judge Scott Beattie said the poll was legally protected speech.

item.title: 英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在 早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員
item.description: [ロンドン ２４日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在　早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員 3:21 配信

２０２３年３月撮影　REUTERS/Hannah McKay

[ロンドン　２４日　ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２４日、米イラン情勢の緊迫化に伴う原油高に伴う英国の長期的なインフレ影響は、エネルギー需要が高まる冬場に顕在化するとの見方を示した。中期的なインフレ要因も年末までに明確になり始めるとし、早期利上げには慎重な姿勢を示した。

英シンクタンクの国立経済社会研究所（ＮＩＥＳＲ） の会議に出席したディングラ氏は、冬場にかけて「賃金交渉の行方や最終的水準についても、より多くのことが分かってくる。金融引き締めはすでに進行中だ」と述べた。

一方、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻を受けてエネルギー価格が急騰した２０２２年のような、広範囲にわたる物価上昇は起きておらず、雇用市場も弱含んでいると指摘した。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）や米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は利上げに動いているものの、英国の需要水準は米国を下回り、指標金利もユーロ圏よりも高いため、英中銀の据え置き決定は妥当だと主張した。ディングラ氏は、今月のＭＰＣで金利据え置きを支持していた。

人工知能（ＡＩ）の利用拡大がサービス部門でのインフレ鈍化につながる可能性があるとの見方も示したほか、英国の中期的なインフレ期待は懸念すべき状況ではないとした。

また、英中銀のロンバルデリ副総裁は２４日、景気減速が鮮明にならない限り、エネルギー価格の高止まりを受けて利上げが必要になるとの認識を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/25(金) 3:21 ロイター

item.title: 約80カ国が国連で共同声明、ホルムズ海峡の再開要求 イランとフーシ派非難
item.description: [国連 ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連　２４日　ロイター] - 世界の約８０カ国は国連で２４日、ホルムズ海峡の緊急再開を求めるとともに、同地域での攻撃や国際貿易・エネルギー安全保障の混乱を巡ってイランとその同盟勢力であるイエメンの武装組織フーシ派を非難した。

バーレーンのザヤーニ外相は共同声明で「ホルムズ海峡におけるイランの行動は、国際的な安全保障および航行の権利と自由を脅かし続けている」と指摘。「またイエメンでの紛争を再開させたフーシ派の決定、サウジアラビアへの継続的な攻撃、紅海における無謀な攻撃についても強く非難する」と述べた。

また、フーシ派がバベルマンデブ海峡に向けて進軍を続けていることは、国際的な海運、海上安全保障、世界貿易に対するリスクを一段と高めるだけだと非難した。

声明には、湾岸アラブ諸国をはじめ主要な西側諸国が賛同した。

item.title: BP eyes Devon Energy asset amid renewed US M&A ambitions, sources say
item.description: BP is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the US, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: David French, Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's (DVN.N) operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the US, people familiar with the matter said. After years of prioritizing investments in renewable energy and leadership churn that included five chief executives since 2020, London-headquartered BP has reverted to a strategy that places its traditional oil and gas business at its heart. Since [USN:L6N40X0S5 TEXT:"Meg O'Neill"] joined as CEO in April, BP has entered the data room on a small number of shale assets placed for sale by their owners, allowing the company access to confidential information provided to prospective buyers so they can evaluate the merits of a deal, according to six sources. BP has targeted predominantly oil-producing assets with valuations of between $2 billion and $5 billion, three of the sources said. This includes Devon Energy's Eagle Ford asset, which opened its data room in late August, said three of the sources. Analysts at TPH Research said in a note on Wednesday the asset could be worth around $4.5 billion. The sources cautioned that entering a data room does not guarantee that BP will formally bid on an asset. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss private deliberations. Shares in Devon extended gains in the wake of the Reuters report, and closed 1.8% higher on Thursday. Devon has risen around 34% this year, per LSEG data. BP declined comment. Devon did not respond to a comment request. BPX ENERGY BP's US shale operations are held within its BPX Energy unit, with assets in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Haynesville basins spanning Texas and Louisiana. Production in the second quarter was around 545,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), of which its existing Eagle Ford was approximately 205,000 boepd, according to an August presentation. The company is targeting over 650,000 boepd from BPX by 2030, according to BP's website. Despite its strategic pivot back to oil and gas, previously overseen by Albert Manifold before he was fired as chair and replaced on a permanent basis earlier this month by [USN:L6N44U0DM TEXT:"Ian Tyler"], BP has spent the last 18 months focused on reducing debt and hitting a [USN:L6N4410CR TEXT:"$20 billion divestment"] target. While it has engaged in some acquisition activity in that time, including showing interest in buying a majority stake in the [USN:L6N40E0X4 TEXT:"Shenandoah field"] in the US Gulf, BP had been largely absent from shale data rooms, making its re-emergence in recent weeks as a potential buyer notable, three of the sources said. Buying assets near its existing footprint would be logical, four of the sources said, given the potential for cost savings and BP's familiarity with local geology. Part of Devon's Eagle Ford asset was held in a joint venture between the company and BP until the partnership's dissolution in 2025. DEVON DIVESTMENT Devon is marketing for sale both its Eagle Ford and Powder River basin acreage in Wyoming, the sources said, as part of a [USN:L4N4411YP TEXT:"portfolio review"] undertaken following its $58 billion merger with Coterra Energy. The Eagle Ford asset consists of around 90,000 net acres, and produced around 77,000 boepd in the second quarter, per Devon's website. The effort comes as U.S. energy assets have increased allure to buyers, as they can operate even as Middle Eastern conflict shakes global oil markets. The tension pushed crude back above $100 per barrel last week, with higher prices of benefit to sellers. Conversely, market volatility makes it harder for buyers and sellers to agree on valuations, as buyers want to avoid the perception of paying an inflated price. Dealmaking involving US production assets has [USN:L6N44211N TEXT:"slumped in recent months"] as a result. This uncertainty is reflected in potential valuations for Devon's Eagle Ford. The TPH Research analysts marked it at $4.5 billion, but the sources pointed to a range between $3.5 billion and roughly $4 billion. Devon is also facing pressure from activist shareholders [USN:L6N42O1EL TEXT:"TOMS Capital"] and [USN:L4N41B1LQ TEXT:"Kimmeridge Energy Management"] to improve performance and shed assets.

WASHINGTON, Sept 24 : The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers until a US review, Politico reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter and a senior US administration official. The White House wants to take steps to make sure US systems are secure before the models are shared with partners, according to the report. The White House, Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The development comes as the White House weighs cybersecurity risks posed by increasingly capable AI models, following a series of incidents in which AI systems gained unauthorized access to real-world computer systems.

item.title: New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights
item.description: The US sanctions aim to stop Iranian airlines from flying worldwide, while Iran warned this could increase tensions in the region.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights

The US sanctions aim to stop Iranian airlines from flying worldwide, while Iran warned this could increase tensions in the region.

Flags are held by Iranian Americans and supporters of the National Council of Resistance of Iran during a march near the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on May 16, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Ken Cedeno)

25 Sep 2026 01:38AM (Updated: 25 Sep 2026 06:36AM)

FAST

DUBAI: Iranian airlines were barred from neighbouring countries including the UAE and Oman on Thurs day (Sep 24) in response to new US sanctions , the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in third countries that do business with Iran. The General Civil Aviation Authority of the United Arab Emirates, the Middle East's biggest travel hub, said that as a result of the new US policy it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines until further notice. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that flights had also been shut down to Oman, Georgia and Azerbaijan, and to the Iraqi capital Baghdad. It said authorities were working to route flights to another Iraqi airport, in Najaf, a major Shi'ite Muslim religious pilgrimage site. Washington had announced it would put sanctions on any global companies doing business with Iranian airlines after Sep 23, with the aim of grounding Iran's entire civil fleet worldwide.

Other countries in the Gulf region also appeared to have restricted flights. Tehran's Imam Khomeini Airport listed scheduled arrivals and departures on Thurs day to and from countries including Afghanistan, Armenia, China, Iraq, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Türkiye. But no flights appeared to be listed to or from the nearby Gulf states, with which Iran has long had some of its most important business and travel ties. Iran has suggested that enforcement of a US-mandated air blockade would lead to potential escalation. On Wednes day , a senior Iranian official threatened to make airports "unusable" in any regional country that abides by the US ban. Separately, on Thurs day , authorities in Saudi Arabia said they had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthi fighters. The Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets. An escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has emerged this month as the combat zone in the wider Middle East war.

"ECONOMIC D- DAY" With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as "secondary sanctions". Trump referred to the new strategy last month as "economic D- Day ", comparing it to the assault on Nazi-controlled France in World War Two by the United States and its allies. A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea. "We are living in an open-air prison," a retired teacher in Tehran told Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.

SAUDI ARABIA SAYS IT SHOOTS DOWN HOUTHI MISSILES The war, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February as "Operation Epic Fury", has disrupted global energy supplies, killed thousands of people and pushed up oil prices. Conflicts have been reignited in other regional countries where Iran has allies, initially in Lebanon and now in Yemen, where the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and launched a lightning advance this month against a Saudi-backed government. The Houthis have repeatedly fired into Saudi Arabia this month, and say the Saudi air force has conducted hundreds of strikes on Yemen since fighting escalated. Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles on Thurs day , after issuing emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red Sea oil port. "Any escalation and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen said in a statement. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had attacked Saudi military sites in Jazan province bordering Yemen, targeting operations rooms, command and control centres, weapons depots, missile launch sites and military camps.

Related:

Iran threatens to expand war to Indian Ocean if US attacks again

Iranian president says he will not allow Strait of Hormuz to be used as leverage

Sources in the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed Yemeni government said their forces had repelled overnight Houthi attacks on a key supply route to Aden, the Indian Ocean port city where the government is based. The Houthis, who already controlled the north including the capital Sanaa, seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast this month and have been pushing into adjacent highlands near the central mountain city of Taiz and the road from Aden. The Houthis have kept up pressure on government forces holding a steep winding mountain pass known as Hejat al-Abd, a lifeline for hemmed in pro-government forces, and for goods entering Taiz. Seizing parts of the Taiz-Aden road could allow the Houthis to tighten their grip around Taiz and deal another blow to the government, which has struggled to regain the initiative since losing the western coast. More than 700 people have been killed and thousands wounded in the latest fighting, according to the United Nations. Nearly 130,000 Yemenis have been displaced within the country, while more than 3,000 have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.content:encoded:
スターバックス、北米で250店閉鎖へ　事業強化策の一環 2:29 配信

米ワシントン州シアトルで2025年11月撮影。REUTERS/Matt Mills McKnight

[２４日　ロイター] - 米コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックスは２４日、北米で業績が低迷する２５０店を閉鎖することを明らかにした。２０２６年９月期末までに大部分の閉鎖を完了させる予定で、約３億ドルの関連費用を見込む。関連当局に書類を提出した。北米にある約１万８０００店のうち約１％に当たるという。２０２４年に就任したブライアン・ニコル最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）による事業強化策の一環。これまでも、創業地である米西部シアトルの旗艦店を含めた北米の不振店の閉鎖に踏み切っている。

世界の直営店・フランチャイズ店の純新規出店数は２６年９月期に約４４０店舗と、従来目標の６００─６５０店舗を下回る見通しだ。ｅＴｏｒｏのグローバル市場ストラテジスト、ラレ・アコナー氏は店舗閉鎖に関して「コストはかかるものの事業再建に向けて理にかなった措置だ」と指摘した。

スターバックスは、米店舗で待ち時間の短縮やメニューの簡素化を通じて人気回復を目指してきた。店舗運営に投資する一方、本社部門の人員削減や一部の地域事務所を閉鎖。直近まで４・四半期連続で既存店売上高が増加していた。ニコル氏は今年４月、すべての所得層で来店客数が増えていると、取り組みへの手応えを示していた。

item.title: RedBird Capital to acquire majority stake in Puck at $250 million valuation, memo says
item.description: RedBird Capital Partners has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Puck in a deal valuing the five-year-old newsletter startup at about $250 million, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RedBird Capital Partners has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Puck in a deal valuing the five-year-old newsletter startup at about $250 million, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Thursday. Reuters first [USN:L6N44M16K TEXT:"reported last month"] that Puck was in advanced talks for an investment from RedBird. The deal will give Puck additional capital to accelerate growth, including by investing further in Air Mail, hiring more talent, entering new markets, pursuing acquisitions and expanding its intellectual property into new formats and channels. Puck acquired Air Mail, the digital magazine founded by former Vanity Fair editor Graydon Carter, last year. RedBird became an investor in Puck after the acquisition. The latest transaction will not change Puck's editorial independence or its business model, according to the memo. Standard Investments and TPG, which have backed Puck since its inception, will exit the company, while RIT Capital will remain a minority investor, alongside RedBird. Employees with vested stock or options will receive a combination of liquidity and continued ownership in the company. Puck and RedBird have also created a new equity incentive plan, the memo said. The transaction is expected to close in about a month, subject to anticipated regulatory approval. Founded in 2021, Puck has built a subscription-based business around journalists with established followings in media, finance, entertainment, fashion and politics.

item.title: Southern California Edison pushing for state wildfire liability deal before legislators depart
item.description: Electric utility Southern California Edison is urging California lawmakers to hold a special session before year-end to consider limiting utilities' exposure to future wildfire liabilities, CEO of parent company Edison International Pedro Pizarro said this week.
item.dc:creator: Laila Kearney
item.content:encoded: Electric utility Southern California Edison is urging California lawmakers to hold a special session before year-end to consider limiting utilities' exposure to future wildfire liabilities, CEO of parent company Edison International (EIX.N) Pedro Pizarro said this week. Electric utility infrastructure has been linked to multiple widespread and deadly California wildfires over the last decade, with the most recent catastrophic Los Angeles fires in January 2025 taking more than two dozen lives, causing billions of dollars in property damage and prompting thousands of lawsuits. Southern California Edison grid equipment is being investigated for causing the Eaton Fire at that time, which started in the Los Angeles County foothills near Altadena. California lawmakers last month failed to pass a plan for how wildfire victims in the state get paid, and what investor-owned electric utilities like Southern California Edison and Pacific Gas & Electric (PCG_pa.A) are on the hook for when their equipment sparks the blazes. A separate, broader, wildfire liability legislative package that was backed by Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom and investor-owned electric utilities in the state also failed to materialize in the weeks prior. Shares of California electric utilities plummeted after the legislative breakdown on concerns the companies could face uncapped wildfire liabilities. Fitch this month also revised down Southern California Edison's credit outlook to negative from stable, which could make borrowing costs higher for the capital-intensive business. Newsom, whose term ends in January, would need to call the special session in the coming months, but quickly reaching a new framework agreement to put before lawmakers could be challenging, Pizarro said. "To get there, that also means we need to push for a deal. Something that's workable, that actually solves a structural issue for California," Pizarro said. That would involve getting various interest groups to agree on a solution, or the framework of a solution, that the legislature could vote on, he said. "If that were the case, I think you could have a pretty targeted special session and get this done," he added. If a special session is not called before the end of the year — and ideally before the November elections — any new wildfire plans will be hammered out by a new governor and many newly elected legislators who will need time to get up to speed on the complex issue that has evolved over years, Pizarro said. "In the meantime, California customers are paying a lot of extra money because of the instability in the market," he said, adding the uncertainty was resulting in hundreds of millions of dollars in additional debt costs.

item.title: フーシ派、サウジ首都リヤドとヤンブー攻撃と表明 南部ジザン州も標的
item.description:
Mohammed Ghobari Timour Azhari
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Ghobari　Timour Azhari

[２４日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２４日、サウジアラビアの首都リヤドの「重要目標」と、紅海沿岸都市ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設をミサイルと無人機（ドローン）で攻撃したと表明した。

サウジは現時点で首都リヤドに対する攻撃があったか確認していない。

これに先立ちフーシ派の軍報道官は、イエメンと国境を接するサウジ南部ジザン州の軍事施設を攻撃したと表明していた。数十発の弾道ミサイルと無人機を使って攻撃を実施し、ジザン州にある「作戦室、指揮統制センター、武器庫」のほか、ミサイル発射拠点や軍事キャンプを標的にしたという。

サウジからこの件に関する確認は得られていない。

サウジ民間防衛当局は２３日にジザンで潜在的な危険があるとして緊急警報を発出していたが、２４日に警報は出されていない。

サウジ主導の連合はこの日、フーシ派が２４日に発射した弾道ミサイル６発を迎撃し、南部タイフと紅海沿岸のヤンブー地区への攻撃を阻止したと明らかにしていた。

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場・午前＝円が159円近辺に下落、9月2日以来の安値
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２４日 ロイター］ - ２４日午前のニューヨーク外為市場では、円が対ドルで下落し、一時９月２日以来の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場・午前＝円が159円近辺に下落、9月2日以来の安値 1:08 配信

2023年3月10日撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

［ニューヨーク　２４日　ロイター］ - ２４日午前のニューヨーク外為市場では、円が対ドルで下落し、一時９月２日以来の安値となる１５８．９８円を付けた。

片山さつき財務相は２４日、円安への対処を巡り「先般の（日米両政府による）協調介入以降のプリンシプル（原則）というのは生きている」と述べたが、日銀の利上げ加速への道筋があると投資家を納得させられなかったことから、地合いはなお弱いままだった。

一方、複数の米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者のタカ派的な発言や堅調な経済成長への期待を受けて、米追加利上げ観測が強まったことを背景に、ドルは２カ月ぶりの高値を付けた。

ＦＲＢが前週に０．２５％の利上げを実施し、政策金利を３．７５─４．００％に引き上げて以降、複数のＦＲＢ当局者が、インフレが鈍化しなければ追加利上げの可能性があると示唆している。

主要通貨に対するドルの値動きを示すドル指数は０．１４％高の１０１．２７。一時１０１．３４まで上昇した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：日米金融政策の転換とドル／円の行方＝植野大作氏 コラム：ドル／円の昨年高値更新に現実味、中立金利や介入効果に注目＝内田稔氏 コラム：有事のドル買いでも堅調維持したユーロ、「筋肉質」な通貨に化けるか＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：「有事のドル買い」と「ドル離れ」の両立、イラン攻撃後の為替相場を読む＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：高市発言受け「ポジティブ修正」、衆院選後のドル／円相場を読む＝尾河眞樹氏 最終更新: 9/25(金) 1:08 ロイター

Study reveals evolutionary history of bats, dating back 65 million years

FILE PHOTO: A Rodrigues fruit bat hangs on a perch in the Masoala Rainforest hall at the zoo in Zurich March 26, 2013. REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: Indian flying foxes or fruit bats are seen as they rest on tree branches inside a temple complex at Kadambazhipuram village in Palakkad district in the southern state of Kerala, India, February 3, 2022./File Photo

FAST

WASHINGTON, Sept 24 : Bats are critical players in global ecosystems, pollinating plants, dispersing seeds and eating huge numbers of insects. One of only three lineages of flying vertebrates in Earth's history, there are more than 1,500 bat species living today. But their evolutionary history has been a bit of a puzzle for scientists.     The largest combined bat genome and fossil study ever conducted is now bringing some clarity. Its findings indicate that these flying mammals first appeared in Europe about 65 million years ago, in the aftermath of the mass extinction event that doomed the dinosaurs, before spreading around the world, not in North America, Asia or Africa as previously hypothesized.     The researchers assembled the largest collection of high-quality bat genomes to date, covering 103 species representing all 21 recognized families of bats. They integrated this data with an analysis of 44 fossil bats to decipher their evolutionary history and generate a bat family tree.     They also concluded that, like flight, echolocation — the biological sonar system many bats use to navigate in the dark and catch flying prey — evolved near the dawn of bat evolution.

"I think being able to do both, fly and echolocate, opens up the most amazing opportunities to move into new niches — hunting at night when there's less competition and fewer predators, for example. Flight got them into the air. Echolocation let them own the night," said Sonja Vernes, a professor of biology at the University of St Andrews in Scotland and one of the leaders of the study published this week in the journal Nature. "Echolocation allowed bats to become nocturnal, essentially, and not compete with birds or be preyed on by diurnal (day-active) birds," said zoology professor Emma Teeling of University College Dublin, another of the study leaders.      The study pointed to bats first appearing in Europe about a million years after an asteroid struck Earth 66 million years ago, a calamity that enabled mammals to become the dominant land animals. Relatively soon thereafter, bats reached Africa, making those two continents a hub of early bat evolution, according to evolutionary biologist Liliana Davalos of the State University of New York at Stony Brook, another of the study leaders. Antarctica is the lone continent bats never inhabited. They now account for more than a fifth of the world's mammal species.     The oldest-known bat fossils date to approximately 52 million years ago. Genome and anatomical data helped identify the origination date of bats. BIRDS AND PTEROSAURS     Bats are the only mammals to have achieved powered flight, joining the flying reptiles called pterosaurs and birds as the only vertebrates to do so. Birds survived the asteroid, but pterosaurs did not. The pterosaur extinction may have opened ecological niches that a new lineage of flying vertebrates could fill. Bat wings, built differently than those of birds and pterosaurs, are modified forelimbs featuring greatly elongated fingers that support a large skin membrane. What the ancestors of bats looked like remains a mystery. "We don't know for sure but I reckon they looked like tree shrews starting to grow long fingers. This is just a guess as all of the oldest fossils look like modern bats," Teeling said. It also is unclear whether flight or echolocation evolved first. Bats use echolocation by making high-frequency ultrasonic sounds and listening to the returning echoes bouncing off objects to chart their surroundings. This ability can be seen in fossils based on anatomical traits such as an enlarged cochlea and specialized middle ear structures. "Our oldest bat fossils show that they had both flight and echolocation capabilities, which doesn't help answer this question. We need to find the oldest 'pre-bats,' or transition fossils, and see if they had anatomical characteristics indicative of flight or echolocation," Teeling said.     Many bat species show remarkable resistance to disease and live exceptionally long lives for their size. The study lays the groundwork for research into the genetic basis of these traits.     "This work could eventually inform human research into aging, immunity and disease resistance," Teeling said. Bats today come in many shapes and sizes, with differing diets and lifestyles. The largest is the giant golden-crowned flying fox of the Philippines, with a wingspan of 5-1/2 feet (1.7 meters). The smallest is the bumblebee bat of Thailand and Myanmar, with a wingspan of about 5 inches (13 cm). Many bats are insectivores. Others consume fruit, nectar, fish and, infamously in the case of vampire bats, blood. There is an amazing array, including the likes of horseshoe bats, leaf-nosed bats, mouse-tailed bats, trident bats, ghost-faced bats, mustached bats, sucker-footed bats, hammer-headed bats and wrinkle-faced bats. "Bats constantly surprise us. They're one of evolution's greatest experiments," Vernes said.

Source: Reuters

Sept 24 : BNP Paribas will keep some sensitive customer data and critical operations off public cloud infrastructure even after signing a five-year cloud and AI partnership with Google, the French bank said on Thursday. The agreement gives BNP access to Google public-cloud infrastructure and Gemini models as the bank develops AI agents for internal work including corporate credit memos, sales, trading, research and structuring. But the deal does not mark a wholesale move, BNP Group Chief Information Officer Marc Camus told reporters in a call. "The fact that we signed this agreement with Google doesn't mean that we will get rid of our on-premise infrastructure," he said.
